Revolving Fund
January 15, 2026
Vermont Department of Environmental Conservation

DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
CONSERVATION LEGISLATIVE REPORT
Annual Report on the Vermont Environmental Protection
Agency (EPA) Pollution Control Revolving Fund
Year: 2026
Date reported: January 15, 2026
Authorizing statute: 24 VSA Ch. 120 Section 4753a(a)
Committees: House Committees on Corrections and Institutions and on Natural Resources,
Fish, and Wildlife and the Senate Committees on Institutions and on Natural Resources and
Energy
Prime contact: Padraic Monks, VT DEC Water Investment Division
Executive Summary
This report provides the General Assembly with an annual summary of loan awards made during the
prior and current fiscal years from the Vermont Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Pollution
Control Revolving Fund, also referred to as the Clean Water State Revolving fund (CWSRF). The purpose
is to report on and seek legislative approval for all the types of projects for which awards are proposed
to be made from the funds for the balance of the current and subsequent fiscal year.
This report includes four tables summarizing loan awards and project types financed through the CWSRF
as follows:
• Table 1: Consists of loan awards made during SFY2025.
• Table 2: Consists of loan awards as of 12/11/2025 for SFY2026.
• Table 3: Consists of a listing of the remaining projects anticipated to be funded in SFY2026,
which may change due to projects being removed or dollar amounts adjusted before
finalization.
• Table 4: Consists of a summary of loan awards projected for the period SFY2025 – SFY2026.
• Table 5: Consists of a description of the types of projects eligible to receive funding through the
CWSRF.
Key Takeaways
• In SFY2025: 50 loans were awarded totaling $42.8 MM, of which 48 are for municipal borrowers
and two are for private borrowers.
• In SFY2026: 11 loans have been awarded to date totaling $16.6 MM, all to municipal borrowers.
A total of approximately $95 MM is available for pending projects. The total pending loan
amount shown in Table 3 is $39 MM.

Annual Report on the Vermont Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Pollution Control
Revolving Fund
January 15, 2026
Vermont Department of Environmental Conservation

• If all current pending loans proceed to award in SFY2026, the two-year total will be $98.5 MM
for 79 projects.
Discussion of Eligible Project Types
Act 185 of 2018 expanded eligibility of the CWSRF to a broader array than previously allowed for
nonpoint source pollution control projects and to private entities. This expanded eligibility is captured
under the term Clean Water Project, which is defined in state statute at 24 V.S.A. §4752(11) and is
included below along with two other relevant statutory terms. These definitions provide the basis for
making CWSRF project eligibility determinations.
"Clean water project" means water pollution abatement and control facilities, as defined in 10 V.S.A. §
1571, and such equipment, conveyances, structural or nonstructural facilities, and natural resources
projects that are needed for and appurtenant to the prevention, management, treatment, storage, or
disposal of stormwater, sewage, or waste, or that provide water quality benefits, including a wastewater
treatment facility, combined sewer separation facilities, an indirect discharge system, a wastewater
system, flood resiliency work related to a structural facility, or a groundwater protection project.
"Water pollution abatement and control facilities" means such equipment, conveyances, and structural
or nonstructural facilities owned or operated by a municipality that are needed for and appurtenant to
the prevention, management, treatment, storage, or disposal of stormwater, sewage, or waste,
including a wastewater treatment facility, combined sewer separation facilities, an indirect discharge
system, a wastewater system, flood resiliency work related to a structural facility, or a groundwater
protection project.
“Natural resources project" means a project to protect, conserve, or restore natural resources, including
the acquisition of easements and land, for the purpose of providing water quality benefits.

Summaries of Loan Awards and Eligible Project Types
Tables 1 through 5, as follows, summarize recent Vermont Clean Water SRF loan activity and eligible
project types. The Vermont Clean Water SRF Program provides funding for planning, design and
construction, referred to as Step 1, Step 2 and Step 3 loans, respectively. In the tables below, the loan
step is indicated in the suffix of the Loan Number. For example, RF1-362-1.1, is a planning, or Step 1
loan: The “-1.” Indicates it is a Step 1 Loan. The “.1” indicates the initial Step 1 loan was amended.
The following abbreviations are used in the Project Descriptions.
CSO - Combined Sewer Overflow Abatement
LTCP -Long Term Treatment Control Plan
NPS - Non-Point Source (soils-based wastewater systems)
PER – Preliminary Engineering Report
PS – Pump Station
SW - Stormwater
WWTF – Wastewater Treatment Facility

areas

water conservation, contaminated sites, landfills, or other groundwater or surface
water projects that would result in a water quality benefit

In November 2022, private equity firm Broad Sky Partners made an undisclosed investment in then-INSIDE Public Accounting top 200 firm Smith + Howard. In the three and a half years since, Smith + Howard has become one of the 85 largest accounting firms in the U.S. based on revenue, sustained organic growth, completed strategic M&A deals, and made investments in technology, core operations, and talent.
And under the leadership of CEO Sean Taylor, Smith + Howard now has approximately 800 professionals across Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Virginia. The firm pulled in revenue of $74.2 million during its most recent fiscal year.
This morning, Smith + Howard announced the next phase of its growth plan, as TPG, a global alternative asset management firm, signed a definitive agreement to make what officials say is a “significant” investment in the Atlanta-based accounting firm. TPG will invest in Smith + Howard through TPG Growth, the firm’s middle-market and growth equity platform.
Financial terms of the deal weren’t disclosed. Smith + Howard will continue to operate under its existing brand and leadership team, according to a June 9 media release.
The transaction is expected to close in the third quarter of this year, subject to customary closing conditions and regulatory approvals.
The deal also is one of the few since private equity firms have bought stakes in accounting firms in which private equity ownership of a firm has transferred, or flipped, from one investment group to another.
The first of this kind was in January 2025 when Blackstone acquired the ownership stake in Citrin Cooperman from New Mountain Capital, a much smaller private equity firm that announced its investment in the New York City-based top 20 accounting firm in April 2022.
Recommended Articles
Smith + Howard says TPG’s investment will bolster its ongoing expansion through investments in operational infrastructure, technology, talent capabilities, enhanced client service offerings, and broader strategic growth initiatives. The partnership will also accelerate the accounting firm’s ongoing efforts to leverage artificial intelligence integration to improve workflows, elevate the client experience, and create additional capacity for professionals as it continues to grow.
Recommended Articles
“We are incredibly proud of what our team has accomplished over the past several years and are grateful to Broad Sky for their partnership during a critical phase of our evolution. Through a combination of organic growth, strategic acquisitions, and continued investment in our capabilities, we have built a stronger, more diversified platform positioned to serve clients at every stage of growth,” Taylor, who has been CEO of Smith + Howard since 2022, said in a statement. “We’re excited to begin our next chapter with TPG. Their experience supporting high-growth professional services businesses, combined with their operational and technology expertise, makes them an ideal partner as we further invest in innovation and growing the firm.”
Founded in 1992 and based in San Francisco, TPG employs 1,900 employees and has 30 offices around the world. The firm manages $306 billion in assets, as of the end of March.
“Smith + Howard has established itself as a highly respected firm, defined by strong client relationships, a partner-led culture, and consistent growth. The firm has demonstrated a clear ability to grow thoughtfully while maintaining the service quality and culture that underpin its success. Its approach to growth, particularly its early investments in technology and AI-enabled capabilities, aligns closely with our business-building model and value creation strategy,” Max Wein, business unit partner at TPG Growth, said in a statement. “We are excited to partner with Sean and the team to build on that foundation and support the firm’s long-term growth strategy.”
Tyler Zachem, CEO and partner at Broad Sky Partners, added: “It has been a privilege to work alongside Sean and the Smith + Howard team. Smith + Howard is emblematic of Broad Sky’s investment strategy; partnering with strong management teams in essential, high-growth professional services markets to build larger, more strategically differentiated platforms. Sean and the team executed at every level, and we are proud of this outcome and excited for what comes next.”
After the closing, Smith + Howard will continue to operate in an alternative practice structure in accordance with applicable professional standards, with Smith & Howard P.C., a licensed CPA firm, providing attest services and Smith & Howard Advisory LLC and its affiliates providing tax, advisory, and other services.

text:
How fast does a distributor have to answer a quote to win?
The first order that came back without a human touching it was a rounding error, and the chief commercial officer put it in front of the board anyway.
At a national distributor of industrial automation components, about one in ten inbound quote requests arrived through the website contact form. AI agents took that queue in late 2025. In the first month they answered more than six thousand emails and returned roughly fifteen hundred quotes, escalating to a human only when it required one.
- Industry
- Industrial automation distribution
- Who uses it
- Inside sales
- What it does
- Inbound quote automation
- Measured
- First 30 days post-launch, late 2025
On a Friday morning in October, the company's chief commercial officer joined a video call with his team and interrupted the agenda to brag.
"We had our first order," he told them. "First order that came through our AI-based system. Literally the automated emails going back and forth, and boom, we got a PO."
It was one purchase order. At a distributor with revenue in the hundreds of millions, that is a rounding error. He called it a historic moment anyway, then asked his team to send him a copy so he could put it on a slide for the board.
To understand why one order mattered that much, you have to understand the situation.
The company distributes the industrial automation components that keep factory floors running. When a machine goes down, a plant manager needs a replacement now, not tomorrow. Several thousand people a day were reaching out across email, phone and the website. That was more than the team could answer.
"We didn't even know how bad it was," the CCO said. "We kind of knew that it sucked, and we were leaving a lot of emails and phones and a lot of revenue on the table."
In a break-fix business, response time is not a service metric. It is the business.
"If you respond within an hour, your probability of getting the business is higher," he said. "It takes two hours, it drops. The third hour, it drops. Anything more than four or five hours, I would say, don't even bother responding."
Chief commercial officer, a national distributor of industrial automation components
Median response time was three to four hours.
Pressure came from several directions at once. The chief executive wanted to move the company from what he called a traditional distributor to a full-blown tech-enabled solutions provider. The private equity sponsor was asking how the company was using AI. And the CCO, five months into the role, had a list of twenty-five things he already knew were broken.
Rather than attack all of it, they took the smallest slice they could find. Quote requests arriving through the website contact form, roughly a tenth of inbound volume.
"We always wanted to spend time here and see if it can work," the chief executive said, "and then start working up the chain from a complexity perspective."
InstaLILY agents took that one queue. They read the incoming request, identify the part, check availability and pricing, and email the customer back. No human in the loop unless the request needs one.
Within two months the company counted more than ten thousand hours a year returned to the business and roughly six inside-sales reps' worth of capacity unlocked without hiring anyone.
The numbers were not why the CCO wanted it. He was blunt with his team about what he was buying. The company has roughly ninety inside sales reps. Some are excellent. Some are not.
"The goal here is not to duplicate what the internal sales rep is doing," he said. "It is what the internal sales rep should be doing."
Take the top twenty reps, figure out what good actually looks like, and encode it, "so the remaining bottom 50, 60, 70 percent come up to that average."
The operations lead running the rollout put the math more plainly. Strip out the research and lookup work so reps can build relationships and chase bigger opportunities. "If we're going to double, we need them to double their efficiency, unless we start cloning them."
Asked what success would ultimately look like, the CCO did not reach for a percentage.
"My nirvana here is zero backlog for every internal sales rep, and the response time is less than one hour."
Measurement window
Website quote queue, first thirty days after launch and first two months after launch, late 2025 into early 2026. Response time baseline measured pre-launch.
Questions this answers
1How quickly does a distributor need to respond to an inbound quote request?
Response probability falls sharply by the hour. This distributor's own read was that a response inside an hour carries the highest win probability, and that past four or five hours it is barely worth responding.
2What share of inbound volume is safe to automate first?
This deployment began with roughly a tenth of inbound volume, the website contact form, chosen specifically as the lowest-complexity queue, then worked up the complexity chain.

publisher: HVAC Technician Shortage: Causes, Impacts, Strategies, & More
text:
Homeowners today take cool air in the summer and cozy heat in the winter for granted, a standard comfort in many houses across the country. Behind every well-regulated home stands a skilled heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) technician who makes it all possible.
Yet not everyone can benefit from indoor air comfort. This isn’t about affordability, but availability: there are simply not enough technicians.
The sad truth is that contractors and service businesses are struggling to find qualified techs, a shortage that’s reshaping the way the industry works.
In this article, we’ll unpack what’s driving the HVAC labor shortage, how it impacts business and clients, and what strategies leaders can use to attract and retain top talent.
What Is the HVAC Technician Shortage?
The HVAC technician shortage refers to the growing gap between demand for HVAC services and the number of qualified technicians available to deliver them.
In short, there are not enough HVAC technicians to fill this role. According to ACHR News, the HVAC industry is dealing with a shortage of 110,000 technicians, with around 25,000 leaving the workforce annually.
As a result, contractors struggle to hire skilled workers fast enough to meet the rising demand as experienced technicians retire.
Why Is There a Shortage of HVAC Technicians?
The HVAC technician shortage has several causes, including:
- An aging workforce: According to data, the average construction worker — including HVAC techs — is nearly 43 years old, which means they’re gradually approaching retirement age. This aging workforce is the main driver of so many job openings, with businesses not finding the right people to fill the gaps.
- Lack of awareness: Younger generations are not aware of how lucrative and promising an HVAC career can be, with high earning potential. As a result, they’re not entering the trades fast enough to replace the retirees.
- Training barriers: Entry requirements, such as licenses and formal training, discourage many who might enter the workforce. Plus, many companies can’t waste time and resources on training new recruits, as they need them to work now.
The #1 newsletter for the trades.
Gregory Vaughan, business manager at an air conditioning company in Queensland, said, “There’s no one in Australia with the skill set who can even do [the job].”
On the other hand, Reddit user Falcon-Simple, who’s contacted around 60 companies, says that no one wants to hire them due to a lack of experience. “I’ll admit I have little experience, but I’m eager to learn. [...] Yet still I’ve only heard back from two, and those are just a maybe.”
- Undervalued trade work and slow career advancement: HVAC is not advertised as an attractive career, unfortunately, as people believe that gaining a college degree is the right way to go.
The HVAC industry is also a physically demanding work environment, often involving unpredictable conditions, hectic work hours, and sometimes even low pay.
Another Reddit user says, “I genuinely thought I would be at least making 60k a year with benefits, but I am struggling to find any company that will take me on for over $20 an hour with two years of service experience in my area.”
Without a clear path, it’s no wonder young people don’t pursue skilled trades like HVAC.
How Severe Is the HVAC Technician Shortage in 2026?
Unfortunately, the HVAC technician shortage has already reached critical levels. The HVAC industry was facing 110,000 unfilled technician positions nationwide almost four years ago, when experts said the shortage could reach 225,000 technicians by 2027, resulting in 1.8 open jobs for every available technician.
More and more people need HVAC services, yet every year, another 25,000 HVAC techs leave the workforce for various reasons (e.g., retirement, burnout, career changes).
Naturally, this shortage affects HVAC businesses, as well as customers. But how, exactly?
Let’s start with HVAC companies.
How Does the Tech Shortage Affect HVAC Businesses?
The shortage affects HVAC businesses on many levels.
First, since there are so many empty spots, projects might take longer than expected, leading to frustrated clients (we’ll get to them later) as delays happen.
On the other hand, companies might book too many jobs as demand rises. This might lead to existing techs and crews being stretched thin, picking up overtime or juggling multiple tasks at the same time, which drives employee burnout and higher turnover.
Costs increase, too. HVAC business owners pay more for unskilled labor and waste time training these new employees.
“We just hired two apprentices, and they are horrible. They want to learn, but you put a tool in their hand and it’s like they’ve never seen it before,” says another Reddit user.
Not to mention the revenue HVAC companies lose when they have to turn down work because there aren’t enough hands available.
In short, it’s increasingly harder for contractors to keep up with customer expectations in an industry that is projected to be worth $445.73 billion by 2033. Reputations are affected, margins suffer, and business growth becomes unachievable.
Now let’s see how this shortage affects clients.
What Are the Consequences for Homeowners and Customers?
For homeowners, the shortage doesn’t necessarily mean a longer waitlist. It affects their comfort, safety, and wallets, too.
Let’s look at Massachusetts, for instance—an area that faces brutal winter conditions and summer heat waves, and where people live in older homes that require year-round HVAC maintenance.
The biggest disruptor is delays. A few years ago, being told to wait weeks for a tech to arrive was unthinkable, so for a state used to same-day service, it means emergency repairs are more difficult to schedule.
There are numbers to back this up. According to FieldBoss, 74 percent of customers expect service within 24 hours if their AC is out. 30 percent want same-day help, while only four percent would wait a week.
Moreover, the cost of HVAC businesses losing a technician falls on the client, translating into higher costs for both routine maintenance and emergency repairs.
Inexperienced technicians and new hires are also a problem, as their overall work might be subpar and jeopardize the safety of homeowners. This puts customers at risk of improper installations or repairs that don’t meet safety standards or the state’s building codes.
And Massachusetts is not the only state facing these challenges. You can find stories of frustrated homeowners everywhere. Which begs the question: just how high is the demand for HVAC technicians?
Are HVAC Technicians in High Demand?
Yes. HVAC technicians are in high demand nationwide. The workforce keeps on growing, with the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reporting that the HVAC workforce is expected to grow by eight percent by 2034 (much faster than average for all industries).
So there will always be a need for skilled HVAC technicians, especially since over 40,000 openings for techs are projected to appear each year due to the need to replace workers who exit the labor force.
Regionally, Florida (38,290), California (34,020), and Texas (32,070) have the highest number of HVAC workers employed, according to an HVAC Classes report.
The states with the highest expected percentage increase of positions for HVAC workers are Utah (34.3 percent), Idaho (26.9 percent), and Montana (26.1 percent), driven by population growth, infrastructure development, and climate-related needs.
As for the states with the highest expected number of new openings, Florida (3,940), California (3,790), and Texas (3,520) dominate the scene.
This surge in demand emphasizes the critical need for skilled HVAC techs to meet evolving demands.
As artificial intelligence advances and is now in our everyday lives, a pressing question arises: in a world already short of HVAC technicians, could AI step in to fill the gap?
Will AI Replace HVAC Technicians?
No, artificial intelligence will not replace HVAC technicians.
However, AI in the trades can support technicians with their work in other ways.
How AI assists HVAC contractors and technicians
AI is here to empower HVAC contractors and technicians, not replace them.
Today’s modern tools can predict maintenance needs before a failure occurs, for example. Or they can streamline routine office tasks like scheduling. AI can also aid in diagnostics, quickly analyzing error codes or system data to help technicians identify problems faster.
Training is also faster. AI-driven simulations allow new hires to practice troubleshooting in a virtual environment.
A practical example is ServiceTitan’s Titan Intelligence.
It’s an AI-driven platform that collects and analyzes data, giving contractors actionable insights into the industry, trends, features, and recommendations for making better business decisions.
Titan Intelligence helps you optimize different parts of your business, such as lowering costs, improving customer experience, and staying competitive in this industry.
You also see how your company compares to similar businesses nationally or regionally, and get pricing suggestions.
Why can’t AI fully replace HVAC technicians?
Many HVAC tasks, like repairing ductwork, require someone to be physically there, as well as manual skills that AI cannot replicate. In addition, complex HVAC systems need critical thinking and on-the-spot problem-solving.
If that’s not enough, clients value human interaction and the ability to speak with someone who can explain and solve the issue. The job also requires a dash of empathy and trust, something that AI can’t fulfill.
Let’s now focus on how you can best work around this tech shortage and soften its effect on your company.
What Strategies Can Solve the HVAC Technician Shortage?
The HVAC labor gap won’t mend itself, so companies must take proactive steps to build a pipeline of talent and retain what they already have.
So, what can you do about this problem? Below are several strategies:
Let’s dissect each of them.
1. Youth recruitment
The youth are the future of the HVAC trade.
Many companies have already started partnering with schools or vocational programs to promote HVAC as a modern, high-tech career, showing students that it’s rewarding and secure work.
So get in front of students and offer them a mentorship, summer program, or scholarships to make the profession more attractive to younger students who don’t know where to go just yet.
Or participate in career fairs and develop apprenticeship programs to attract the right candidates.
2. Improved training programs
Another thing you can do is provide vocational training programs to bring new hires up to speed.
Employers who prioritize training will enjoy higher retention and faster productivity gains, as they’ll have an apprentice that they can rely on when work piles up fast.
Make sure that your programs focus on real-world applications, which helps new recruits transform theory into practice. Moreover, aligning your training with HVAC-required certifications makes it more meaningful.
3. Incentives and sign-on bonuses
Money talks. Acknowledging a technician’s extra effort with a bonus isn’t just you being nice. It shows appreciation and plays a huge role in attracting and retaining HVAC talent.
Here are some reward ideas:
- Performance-based bonuses
- Profit-sharing programs
- Tuition reimbursement for continuing education
- Access to physical therapy
- Wellness programs
- Paid certifications
- Comprehensive healthcare
Going the extra mile to motivate your techs boosts productivity and employee satisfaction. By linking rewards directly to performance and career growth, you create a win-win system that drives loyalty while strengthening your workforce.
Upfront incentives like sign-on bonuses show immediate value to potential candidates who already weigh multiple offers. Even a modest bonus can tip the scales in your favor. Bonus points if you promise rewards at different milestones, as it can help reduce turnover in the future.
Overall, not only does offering cash incentives lead to great applicant interest, but it also signals that your business values skilled labor and is willing to invest in a long-term relationship.
4. Flexible schedules
The HVAC industry is not for the faint of heart. In this physically demanding field that requires techs to spend overtime and be available during seasonal surges or emergencies, offering flexible scheduling can be a powerful tool to retain technicians.
Offer options like four-day workweeks, alternating shifts, or guaranteed weekends off to reduce burnout and improve work-life balance—a thing which the younger generation will appreciate.
Flexibility shows respect for the technicians’ personal lives, which builds loyalty and reduces turnover.
These methods will help you recruit younger people by making the HVAC field more attractive and promising to them.
Now, let’s move on to what you can do to improve technician retention.
How Can HVAC Businesses Improve Technician Retention?
Recruiting new technicians is only part of solving the HVAC technician shortage. The bigger challenge is keeping the talent you already have.
Here’s what you can do to prevent skilled HVAC workers from leaving:
1. Invest in user-friendly tools
HVAC technicians are nothing without their tools, and they’re more likely to stay with companies that give them the equipment they need to succeed.
Outdated or clunky systems slow down work, waste valuable time, and create frustration, leading to technicians leaving for greener pastures.
Offering user-friendly software simplifies tasks, reduces paperwork, and lets techs focus on what they do best: solving issues and serving customers. For instance, platforms like ServiceTitan provide mobile-friendly interfaces for scheduling, invoicing, and reporting—in short, giving them everything they need at their fingertips.
2. Create a positive company culture
While pay and perks matter, culture is another defining factor for retention. After all, no one likes to work in a toxic environment, especially if they’re never rewarded for their extra effort.
Companies recognizing achievements create a sense of belonging and make technicians feel valued as people.
A positive and supportive culture is where people feel respected, heard, and appreciated. That’s why companies should recognize achievements to create a sense of belonging and make technicians feel valued, and encourage open communication where people can share ideas and concerns without fearing repercussions.
In a nutshell, a positive culture reduces stress and burnout, especially during peak HVAC seasons.
3. Offer clear career paths
Some technicians might leave a company because they’re tired of being stuck in the same role. There are no clear advancement paths, so workers are not motivated to do their best or stick with the business.
Have a structured progression plan in place and let your technicians know about it. For example, they could start as an apprentice and then become a lead tech, before moving on to supervisory, operations, or even sales roles.
When technicians see a future beyond the day-to-day grind, they’re more likely to stay, invest in their skills, and view your company as a long-term partnership.
4. Provide a transparent payroll
Uncertainty around paid hours, commissions, or bonuses leads to mistrust and pushes technicians to look elsewhere for clearer and consistent pay structures.
Clearly outlining how pay is calculated, whether performance-based, hourly, or flat rate, is essential for retention because it helps techs feel confident they’re being compensated fairly.
So, when payroll is transparent and accurate, companies foster trust, reduce disputes, and build loyalty among employees.
5. Implement work-life balance policies
HVAC means long hours, emergency calls, and busy peak seasons, which can quickly lead to burnout. To retain your top talent, you should implement some policies that give techs time to recharge.
This might include:
- Flexible scheduling
- Guaranteed time off
- Rotating on-call duties
- Mental health support programs
Those who feel their personal lives are respected are more engaged with their workplace. It also leads to higher productivity, fewer absences, and long-term retention.
Next, we’ll examine how technology can help with the tech shortage.
How Can Technology Help HVAC Businesses Overcome the Shortage?
Modern platforms like ServiceTitan can help solve the HVAC tech shortage by giving contractors the tools to maximize efficiency, reduce administrative burden, and use their technician roster to its full potential.
Smarter Scheduling & Dispatch
When technicians are in low supply, scheduling becomes more critical than ever. ServiceTitan’s scheduling and dispatching software centralizes all job details, assignments, and customer arrival windows in one easy-to-use user interface.
With intelligent schedule optimization, route planning, and real-time updates, managers can see each technician’s route, job duration, and service type, and reduce double bookings while keeping teams flexible.
ServiceTitan’s Adaptive Capacity takes this further by overlaying live technician capacity against each time window. The system displays both capacity percentage and number of available techs in real time, allowing dispatchers to assign work where it fits best.
As a result, Adaptive Capacity ensures optimal coverage, maximizes the impact of each technician, and helps businesses respond dynamically to urgent requests, reducing wait times for clients and travel time.
Self-Serve Booking & Proactive Text/Email Updates
If you want to deliver unmatched customer service, then ServiceTitan is for you. Through its customer portal, you give customers 24/7 access to make payments, self-schedule, and reduce the administrative burden on your workers.
This feature gives clients the flexibility to book when it’s convenient for them, which in turn reduces the volume of incoming calls for your customer service representatives.
As a result, it frees staff to focus on higher-value tasks, such as complex service requests that can’t be solved through a phone call.
That’s not all—once scheduled, ServiceTitan automatically sends proactive text and email notifications to keep customers informed about technician details, arrival windows, or changes to the schedule.
This transparency is greatly appreciated by your customers, increasing their satisfaction and reducing no-shows, while alleviating the burden for your office staff.
Mobile Field App
ServiceTitan’s Field App lets you upload your own forms and pricebooks and helps teams secure more sales and get rid of outdated clipboards.
The App also equips techs with the information they need while in the field, reducing the back-and-forth between them and the office. Techs can quickly access client and equipment history, giving them context on past repairs, warranties, and recurring issues.
It also allows them to complete digital forms on-site, eliminating paperwork and ensuring accurate records for billing. Moreover, if techs lose or forget an important document, they’ll find it in the app immediately.
ServiceTitan Mobile allows companies to build estimates directly from the pricebook items or proposal templates. They can browse photos, videos, and product information to build a personalized estimate for the customer. As for the customer, they get a clear, professional option right on the spot, which helps speed up the decision process.
Visibility & Back-Office Efficiency
With ServiceTitan, people in the trades can enhance back-office operations by using real-time dashboards and technician scorecards that track performance across the business.
Through this dashboard, managers can see which techs are performing well, identify bottlenecks, and monitor service quality. If someone falls short of required standards, companies can enable data-driven coaching and new training opportunities.
Scorecards are not only for technicians, but also allow office staff to track metrics like first-time fix rates, average job duration, and customer satisfaction scores.
With these insights, you can determine where crews can take on more work (without overwhelming them) or might need additional support. In addition, by highlighting trends, businesses can reduce callbacks, optimize scheduling, and improve customer service.
How Can HVAC Businesses Future-Proof Themselves?
To combat the HVAC technician shortage, businesses must take a proactive approach to recruiting younger people and retaining existing staff.
Investing in technology such as ServiceTitan streamlines workflows, allowing techs to do their job more efficiently. Moreover, developing strong training programs, creating clear career paths, and providing flexible schedules will help attract skilled staff.
Companies that use these strategies can reduce burnout and adapt quickly to industry changes, creating the path to a more sustainable future.

Middle market M&A activity weakened in the third quarter of 2025 showed signs of the typical late summer slowdown. Although the number of deals reported fell 20%, reported multiples increased 9% from 6.9x to 7.5x quarter-over-quarter. Similarly, deal value and transaction volume was up from the previous quarter, with total deal value reaching its highest level since the fourth quarter of 2024. The third quarter of 2025 experienced renewed activity in leveraged recapitalizations and growth financings, leading to larger, better-capitalized businesses able to support higher leverage levels.
Credit conditions continued to stiffen modestly as overall debt utilization decreased in the third quarter, bringing the year-to-date debt-to-EBITDA average down to 3.8x from 4.0x in the first half of 2025. Continuing a recent trend, lenders are demanding higher equity contributions and applying stricter underwriting standards, reflecting heightened borrowing costs and cautiousness.

text:
WPP PLC
07 August 2024
| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE | 7 August 2024 |
WPP plc ("WPP" or the "Group")
WPP to sell its majority stake in FGS Global at an Enterprise Value of $1.7bn, unlocking significant value for its shareholders
WPP plc (LSE/NYSE: WPP) today announces it has entered into an agreement to sell its entire majority stake in leading strategic communications and advisory firm, FGS Global ("FGS" or the "Firm"), to Kite Bidco Inc., an entity controlled by investment funds managed or advised by Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co. L.P. ("KKR") (the "Transaction"). KKR first made a minority investment in the Firm in July 2023.
The Transaction accelerates the value realisation for WPP from its strategic advisory businesses. This strategy started with the merger of Finsbury, The Glover Park Group and Hering Schuppener in 2021, the subsequent acquisition of Sard Verbinnen in 2021 and the introduction of KKR as a minority shareholder in 2023. Through these transactions, FGS has become a global leader in providing advice to the stakeholder economy with over 1,400 experts and over 1,600 clients.
This Transaction better positions WPP to focus on and invest in its world-class creative, media and corporate and consumer public relations businesses to deliver growth while strengthening the Group's balance sheet.
The consideration for the sale of WPP's c.50% stake at an Enterprise Value of $1.7bn (c.£1.3bn1) is $775m (£611m) ($707m (£557m) after tax) payable in cash at completion2. This represents an attractive valuation multiple to the 2023 EBITDA.
The total cash proceeds payable on completion of $767m (£604m)3 will be used to reduce WPP's leverage, implying pro-forma average net debt to EBITDA of c.1.60x4. WPP aims to continue to manage its debt within the targeted range of 1.5-1.75x average net debt to EBITDA, enabling it to invest in the growth of its businesses, pay dividends and return surplus capital to investors over time. The Transaction has no impact on WPP's current year or medium-term guidance and is expected to be broadly earnings neutral in 2025.
The Transaction is expected to close before the end of 2024, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions. The Transaction is a related party transaction, falling within UK Listing Rule 8.2.1R, due to KKR's existing c.28% shareholding in FGS. The board of WPP (the "Board"), which has been so advised by Goldman Sachs International, acting in its capacity as sponsor, considers that the terms of the Transaction are fair and reasonable as far as WPP shareholders are concerned. In giving its advice, Goldman Sachs International has taken account of the Board's commercial assessment of the Transaction. The Board considers the Transaction to be in the best interests of WPP shareholders as a whole.
Mark Read, CEO of WPP, said: "The sale of FGS represents an excellent outcome for WPP. Together with the management of FGS we have built a world-leading strategic communications and advisory group, creating considerable value for all stakeholders. We have achieved an attractive price, enabling WPP to accelerate the crystallisation of the significant value created. This also provides WPP with greater financial and management flexibility as we continue to grow our core business including Burson and Ogilvy Public Relations which give our clients access to world-class public relations services."
Alexander Geiser, Global CEO of FGS, added, "Over the past four years, we have built one of the world's leading strategic communications and advisory businesses from three independent consultancies and the addition of Sard Verbinnen. I would like to thank WPP for their help and long-standing collaboration in growing our firm. We are thrilled by the continued support of KKR, who also share our vision and strategy to be the leading advisor helping clients navigate the increasingly complex stakeholder economy. KKR's exceptional investment track record, extensive experience and global resources will be invaluable as we further grow our integrated solutions globally as a standalone firm."
Philipp Freise, Partner and Co-Head of European Private Equity at KKR, stated: "Our investment in FGS reflects our strong commitment to strategic partnerships, where we provide long-term capital and global resources to entrepreneurial teams and world-class businesses. We strongly believe in FGS's strategy and leadership and have been pleased with our partnership since our minority investment in July 2023. In today's increasingly complex stakeholder ecosystems, the value of FGS's insight, advice and execution is increasingly essential for organizations to navigate uncertainty and achieve their goals. We look forward to continuing our collaboration and helping FGS realize their vision as a global category leader."
1 $ enterprise value and consideration translated into £ at an exchange rate of £1:$1.27
2 Assuming a 30 November 2024 completion date; exact proceeds will vary slightly with completion date
3 Comprising £557m consideration (after tax) for WPP's c.50% stake as well as a net £47m inflow for the repayment of a loan made by WPP to FGS, less FGS's cash on balance sheet
4 Pro-forma average adjusted net debt to headline EBITDA (last 12 months) (including depreciation of right-of-use assets) of c.1.60x, versus WPP's average adjusted net debt to headline EBITDA (last 12 months) (including depreciation of right-of-use assets) of c.1.84x at 30 June 2024. Calculated by reducing WPP's average adjusted net debt over the last twelve months by the expected cash proceeds after tax of c.£604m and reducing headline EBITDA by FGS's headline EBITDA contribution.
About WPP:
WPP is the creative transformation company. We use the power of creativity to build better futures for our people, planet, clients and communities. For more information, visit www.wpp.com.
About FGS:
FGS Global is the world's leading strategic communications and advisory firm, with approximately 1,400 professionals around the world, advising clients in navigating complex stakeholder situations and reputational challenges. FGS Global was formed from the combination of Finsbury, The Glover Park Group, Hering Schuppener and Sard Verbinnen & Co to offer board-level and c-suite counsel in all aspects of strategic communications - including corporate reputation, crisis management and government affairs - and is also the leading force in financial communications worldwide.
FGS Global offers seamless and integrated support with offices in the following locations: Abu Dhabi, Amsterdam, Beijing, Berlin, Boston, Brussels, Calgary, Chicago, Dubai, Dublin, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Hong Kong, Houston, Kingston, London, Los Angeles, Munich, Paris, Riyadh, San Francisco, Shanghai, Singapore, Tokyo, Toronto, Washington, D.C., South Florida, Vancouver and Zurich. The firm is headquartered in New York.
In 2023, FGS generated $465m (£374m) of net sales, $90m (£72m) headline EBITDA (including depreciation of right-of-use assets) and $87m (£70m) headline operating profit, which WPP fully consolidated given its controlling stake.
About KKR:

text:
The Indian tech industry is projected to reach $300 billion revenue in FY26, a Nasscom report said on Monday, adding that in the current fiscal (estimated), the industry will add at least 126,000 net new employees, taking the total workforce to 5.8 million.
Amid shifting global economic patterns and evolving market dynamics, the current fiscal (FY25) has been a year of strategic resilience, with segments such as engineering R&D and global capability centres (GCCs) driving growth for the technology industry in India.
According to the 'Annual Strategic Review 2025' by the IT industry's apex body, growing at 5.1 per cent, the tech industry added $13.8 billion incremental revenue, taking the total industry revenue to over $282.6 billion (including hardware), in FY2025E.
India's digital economy driven by sustained growth in domestic tech spending outpaced export growth for the second consecutive year, with domestic tech revenues registering a 7 per cent annual increase from FY24.
The momentum has been further driven by increased adoption of enterprise software and cloud solutions, alongside a 21 per cent growth in data centre capacity driving increased investments, the report mentioned.
"Enhanced AI implementation, rise of Agentic AI disrupting business models, and increasing maturity of GCCs as hubs for value and transformation are driving the industry shifts," Nasscom Chairperson Sindhu Gangadharan said.
As technology becomes deeply intertwined with global geopolitics and trade dynamics, enterprises must prioritise tech skills transformation within the workforce.
"Building resilient organisations and investing in digital trust will be critical to shaping these trends and sustaining the tech industry's long-term growth," she mentioned.
The broader digital economy now contributes an estimated 12 per cent to the GDP, with Digital Public Infrastructure adding a 1 per cent value boost.
E-commerce continues to expand rapidly, growing at a 35 per cent annual rate, with projected gross merchandise value (GMV) nearing $200 billion.
Nasscom President Rajesh Nambiar said that India's tech skill intensity will be a critical driver of future growth.
While overall AI adoption remains measured, over 55 per cent of AI activity by Indian tech services firms focused on building long-term co-creation partnerships to develop scalable, future-ready AI solutions.
(With inputs from IANS)
title: Indian IT industry to hit $300 bn revenue in FY26, workforce to reach 5.8 mn in FY25; Report

ServiceTitan clients who are Pricebook Pro users have a higher average ticket size and their revenue has grown faster in 2020 than those who do not use Pricebook Pro, the company’s industry-wide data shows.
The numbers come despite the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on businesses in the U.S. and elsewhere.
Pricebook Pro simplifies pricebook management for contractors, allowing pricebooks to stay up-to-date with new pricing, descriptions and images. The platform allows technicians to create good-better-best options for consumers and easily present upgrades and recommendations to maximize ticket size.
ServiceTitan studied the year-over-year data of 179 clients who have been using Pricebook Pro since 2019. The data shows revenue for 2020 has increased by 12% for Pricebook Pro users — vs. 2% for non-users.
In terms of ticket size, the average ticket size for contractors using Pricebook Pro grew at 14% year-over-year, as compared to 8% for non-users. The average ticket size for Pricebook Pro users was about $34 higher in 2020, through mid-April.

text:
Television has always been considered one of the most expensive advertising mediums, reserved solely for the ‘big boys’ with huge media budgets and eye-watering production costs. Think of the news generated by Super Bowl ads before they even run.
But with Connected TV, the rules have changed. How much does it cost to advertise on CTV? Keep reading our article to find out!
How much does it cost to advertise on CTV vs. on linear TV? On paper, the rates for CTV advertising are higher than the median CPM (Cost-Per-Thousand) for linear television, which hovers between $10 and $15. The average CPM for YouTube videos, on the other hand, runs at $20 to $25, and that of CTV can range from $35 to $65.
But CPMs aren’t the way to measure ROI. CTV advertising offers a level of targeting that is simply inconceivable from linear TV ads. This gives CTV the edge in terms of cost performance. In fact, consumers typically view up to 95% of the CTV ads they are exposed to, bringing down the CPCV (Cost-Per-Completed-View) significantly.
In addition, linear TV advertising requires advertisers to pay whether the viewers are interested in the ad or not. With CPCV programmatic campaigns, on the other hand, audiences must watch at least 30 seconds worth of the video ad – and sometimes even the full ad – to be counted as a ‘view’. This means that viewers who only watch part of an ad or skip it altogether do not affect the cost of the campaign, and advertisers are charged only when the ad performs.
If you’re wondering, ‘How much does it cost to advertise on CTV?’, you’ll probably want to know about OTT as well. CTV advertising allows you to run your ads on multiple connected devices, including smart TVs with a built-in Internet connection and TVs that get their connection through an external device or a connected gaming console.
OTT refers to programming that is watched through a connected device such as a smartphone, a tablet, or a computer. It doesn’t include television sets, unless they are equipped with a CTV dongle (Roku or Amazon Fire Stick, for example) to stream video content from a connected device or a computer. OTT commercials can be shown on multiple streaming platforms, including Hulu, ESPN, HBO Now, and more.
How much does it cost to advertise on CTV and run your ads on Hulu, Roku, or on YouTube?
Many factors go into running a CTV ad, so costs tend to vary considerably. One of the main elements to consider is your audience, based on your specific niche as well as where you wish to run your ad. The larger the relevant audience, the higher the cost, which is also why a CTV ad will have a greater CPM than a local TV spot.
Demand can also make CTV advertising rates fluctuate. Using the Vibe platform will help you set a daily budget for your campaign. You can also determine a fixed amount to be spent over the duration of the entire campaign. Instead of having to measure how much it costs to advertise on CTV and to keep an eye on CPM fluctuations, you have full control over your spend.
Connected TV offers a number of benefits for advertisers, including more budget flexibility; and with the rise of programmatic buying, connected TV ads are easier to buy and place than ever before.
How much does it cost to advertise on CTV successfully? Well, it all depends on what your expectations are; but what makes connected TV ads so unique is that you can get a significant return on your investment regardless of how much (or how little) you spent in the first place. By setting your own rules, you can allocate your budget as you see fit, giving you the flexibility to refine your strategy as you go, without any constraints.
Flexible budgeting and the ability to tailor your advertising strategy to your own needs makes CTV a particularly attractive option for those looking to get the most out of their advertising dollars.
While ‘traditional’ linear TV requires huge budgets up front, often ranging in the several hundreds of thousands of dollars, Connected TV delivers brands and marketers flexibility, accessibility and simplicity.
Technically, you could spend only $100 on CTV advertising, but that wouldn’t be the smartest or most effective business decision. The minimum budget really depends on the target population you’re trying to reach. You can reach a narrow target within a well-defined, specialized niche for just a few thousand dollars, whereas a national ad campaign on premium broadcast networks in prime time will cost millions of dollars.
Conversely, Vibe affords you the freedom to run ads on premium TV content from CNN, National Geographic or the NFL without blowing your budget as opposed to enormous budgets and huge guaranteed buys on traditional TV.
With connected TV, you have the power to control the budget of your ad campaigns. You can set a limit on how much you’re willing to spend on each ad, choose to target specific viewers to ensure that your message is seen by the right people, and therefore control your budget more effectively.
Once you’ve decided your budget, you’ll need to determine the CPM (Cost per thousand) you’re willing to pay. CPM is another term from the ad world, where the M is actually mille (thousand) just like in Roman numerals. When buying digital advertising on the open web, marketers set the price they’re willing to pay per thousand impressions. Vibe’s powerful bidding algorithm gets you the best price per mille every time. You can also do this via search engine ads and other PPC (pay-per-click) platforms.
With Connected TV, we see the CPM vary anywhere from $10 all the way up to $70, and the average is usually around $30. The CPM you’ll need to pay greatly depends on the content – and therefore the viewers – you’re targeting. Some channel providers demand a high CPM, while others are less restrictive.
As this article has hopefully demonstrated, CTV is for just about every brand and every marketer. You needn’t worry about your budget, just get started and see how easy it is!

text:
The Lead
Leftover LIHEAP funds used to give Pennsylvania enrollees $100 supplemental benefit
Roughly 139,000 low-income Pennsylvanians will get a LIHEAP supplemental benefit worth $100 to reduce their utility bills. (Photo by Dave Cummings/New Hampshire Bulletin)
Just over two-thirds of low-income Pennsylvanians who tapped a federal fund to pay utility bills over the winter will get a supplemental benefit.
It started July 29 and the assistance is tailored to target the most vulnerable residents.
The state Department of Human Services said the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), which is entirely funded by federal dollars, started with $232 million ahead of the program’s 2025-2026 season, which ended in early May.
Energy assistance need ‘tremendous’ in Pa., but shutdown halts delivery of critical funds
“We know that even though winter is over, many Pennsylvanians may still need assistance with utility bills from last season. LIHEAP helps some of the Commonwealth’s most vulnerable citizens – children, older Pennsylvanians, people with disabilities, and low-income families – make ends meet and keep their homes safer, and we are pleased to be able to offer this one-time supplemental payment to LIHEAP households,” said Human Services Secretary Dr. Val Arkoosh in a release.
More than 278,000 households received benefits over the winter, but the $100 supplement benefit will target 193,000 households that have at least one family member who has a disability, is age 60 or older, or is a child under the age of six. Families don’t need to apply and the payments will go directly to their utility company or home heating provider.
The minimum LIHEAP cash grant is $200 and the maximum is $1,000. Applicants can also secure crisis assistance and weatherization grants.
Receiving the $100 LIHEAP supplemental benefit will not impact future program eligibility. Pennsylvania received $231 million in LIHEAP funds for the 2024-2025 season.
The average benefit that year was $336 for 303,000 households.
