text:
Never miss a call again.
Whether you use Contact Center Pro or a separate third-party phone system, ServiceTitan’s AI Virtual Agents help your team book more jobs by handling overflow, after-hours calls, and routine scheduling—automatically.
In a recent webinar, ServiceTitan CEO & Co-Founder Ara Mahdessian and Product Director Henry Cheng take a deep dive into AI Virtual Agents—ServiceTitan’s newest innovation built for smarter scheduling, faster service, and always-on support.
Native, enterprise-grade, and purpose-built for the trades, AI Virtual Agents turn every call into revenue.
In this recap, we’ll cover:
- Why all businesses should use AI Virtual Agents
- What makes ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agents unique
- What our AI Virtual Agents can do today
- How to launch your own AI Virtual Agent in ServiceTitan in minutes
- New AI Virtual Agent features coming in Q1 of 2026
With AI (artificial intelligence) changing how every business in every industry operates, now’s the time for companies to tap into that powerful automation to deliver a better customer service experience and increase profits.
“We want to make sure the trades are leading from the front,” says Mahdessian. “Whether it’s through our AI solutions or it’s through AI solutions from our partners, we want to make sure that we help democratize access to this powerful technology.”
“We want to make sure our customers are never left behind, and we want to see you guys continue to further your already very impressive success,” he adds.
Why all businesses should use AI Virtual Agents
“Every call that comes into our business is worth anywhere between a few hundred dollars to several thousands of dollars,” Mahdessian says. “So, we want to make sure to maximize call booking rates and capture every single call that comes our way.”
Unfortunately, in today’s fast-paced digital world, companies struggle to answer every single call 24/7. It’s hard to hire, train, and retain high-performing CSRs, and current solutions on the market leave contractors searching for better options.
- Unanswered calls to your business means missed revenue.
- Staffing shortages during busy times means missed calls + lost revenue.
- Third-party answering services just don’t cut it for the trades.
“If we can improve call booking rates by 10%, that typically means we can also increase revenue by about 10%, and often means we can actually increase profit by more than 10%,” Mahdessian says.
That’s where ServiceTitan’s AI Virtual Agents come in. ServiceTitan customers asked for integrated virtual agents to increase their call booking rates. Virtual agents answer calls received after hours and on the weekends, and also help during regular business hours when you suddenly receive an influx of calls and struggle to answer every one.
“It’s very hard in any seasonal business to staff at the peak of call volume,” Mahdessian says. “Many of those calls go unanswered.”
How ServiceTitan Virtual AI is unique
ServiceTitan Virtual AI is built for every type of business, from small, family-owned businesses to large, private-equity-backed businesses. Now, it has the ability to book or reschedule a job, answer questions about a job or invoice, or provide information about your products and services.
“The goal here is to maximize call booking rates,” Mahdessian says. “You have to get the tone and the style right. It has to sound human-like, but you also need to be able to handle all types of requests.”
To maximize call booking rates, you need real-time capacity to ensure jobs are booked at the right time. Otherwise, you’ll end up manually calling customers and rescheduling jobs, which creates extra work for your back office and results in a poor customer experience.
So how are ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agents different from the rest?
- They are the only virtual agents that integrate with adaptive capacity directly inside of ServiceTitan.
- You can set up and launch your own virtual agent in just a few minutes, automatically integrating it with your existing tech schedules, zones, or job types.
- The virtual agent automatically updates itself with no extra work on your part. Since it’s natively in ServiceTitan, you don’t need to manage data in two different systems.
What AI Virtual Agents can do for your business today
Regardless of your phone system—whether you use Contact Center Pro, Phones Pro, or a third-party phone system—ServiceTitan Virtual AI provides a slew of features right out of the box.
New ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agent features include the ability to:
- Confirm appointments
- Reschedule appointments based on capacity
- Book membership maintenance appointments
AI Virtual Agents understand which customers are valued members, and can thank them for being a valued member for a specific number of years.
Powerful customization tools to keep ServiceTitan Virtual AI fully under your control include:
Job booking customization: Since AI Virtual Agents are built directly in ServiceTitan, you can customize and select which job types the virtual agents can and can’t book, down to the business unit, Cheng says. You can set a custom dispatch fee and a message communicating the dispatch fee terms for every job type or business unit combination.
Live escalation: If a customer doesn’t want to talk to a virtual agent, or the agent cannot handle the call, the virtual agent can escalate the call to a human team member, cellphone number, or a third-party answering service. “You will always have peace of mind that no matter what happens at any time of the day, the virtual agent can always get in touch with someone,” Cheng says.
Call classification: The virtual agent classifies its own calls, so it ties booked calls to jobs. It also marks confirmations and rescheduled jobs as excused and links it to the appropriate job record. It classifies unbooked calls and classifies spam or other calls as not a lead. This ensures accurate data in the virtual agent scorecard.
ServiceTitan enables businesses to customize all of these directly within the platform interface.
“You get to train the AI yourself and teach the AI what each job type is used for,” Cheng says. This ensures the virtual agent accurately identifies the right job type, every single time.
Now ServiceTitan customers have additional tools to customize AI virtual agents.
A self-service knowledge base functions as your own repository where a virtual agent can automatically retrieve information. You can upload business files about your membership plan, current and ongoing promotions or coupons, what customers can expect during a tech visit, or answers to common questions your CSRs receive.
A custom follow-up question tool enables you to customize generic virtual agent questions so you can get the information you need for your dispatchers and technicians.
“All of this is fully within your control,” Cheng says.
ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agents deliver improved results
The best news of all? ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agents deliver results.
“We are seeing the virtual agents perform at similar or better booking rates than human agents,” Cheng says.
Statistics show the virtual agents perform at a 70% booking rate when including capacity-related issues. This includes situations when a customer wanted an earlier appointment that wasn’t available. Without capacity issues, the virtual agent had a 90% booking rate.
Another early adopter booked more than 500 jobs with ServiceTitan AI Virtual Agents in the past 30 days — representing 23% of their total jobs for the month.
“This technology is already driving real results that lead to real revenue and real efficiency gains,” Cheng says. “This is a win-win-win situation no matter how you look at it.”
How to launch your own AI Virtual Agent in ServiceTitan
ServiceTitan makes it easy to set up your own customized virtual agent using Contact Center Pro, Phones Pro, or any phone provider you currently use. Businesses do not need a commitment to start using virtual agents, and pay a per-call usage fee.
You’ll use a specific virtual agent phone number and set up rules for when virtual agents answer calls, such as during closed business hours, or during office hours if no one answers the call within 60 seconds.
To ensure virtual agent success, it’s key to set up capacity to ensure the virtual agent has accurate, real-time data to provide the best time slots for customers who want to schedule an appointment. Creating strategic rules for adaptive capacity ensures the virtual agent books high-priority jobs and boosts revenue.
Add custom follow-up questions to help the virtual agent figure out which job type to use. For instance, you can train virtual agents to ask about the age of the HVAC unit or if a water leak is affecting the entire house.
And when a customer asks about a price, a virtual agent can respond, “Every home is different. The best way for us to provide an accurate estimate is to get one of our professionals out there. Would you like to proceed with that?”
Keep tabs on virtual agent performance through virtual agent scorecards within ServiceTitan. You can review calls, call summaries, and performance in the same way you review the performance of your human agents.
>> Want to see how to set up virtual agents step-by-step? Check out the on-demand webinar to watch the demo.
The #1 newsletter for the trades.
New AI Virtual Agent features coming in Q1 of 2026
New features are coming within the following weeks and months.
“This is really just the very, very beginning,” Cheng says. “These virtual agents are going to improve dramatically faster than anything you have ever seen.”
Look for these new AI Virtual Agent features:
- A dedicated virtual agent dashboard to better monitor virtual agent performance, including more reports and insights.
- Multi-agent support to set up multiple virtual agents with an account. This will allow businesses to test different settings and configurations to continuously optimize results.
- Export virtual features to SMS so virtual agents can respond to customers through text.
- Speed to lead with AI to get immediate results from lead-generation platforms like Angi or Thumbtack.
- Multi-point escalation to help virtual agents escalate calls to different people and departments.
- Real-time monitoring and control for improved visibility through live transcripts, sentiment, call reasons, and the ability to take over a call in real time.
- ServiceTitan payment integration to give the virtual agent the ability to collect payment over the phone through an SMS link if the customer has a payment on file.
- An AI command center to track your AI journey along with your human teams across multiple parts of your business.
Ready to learn more? Check out the following resources:
- How to Set up your AI Virtual Agent for a personalized customer experience
- How to configure AI Virtual Agents for Basic Phones and Phones Pro
- How to configure your AI Virtual Agent settings in Contact Center Pro
Call (562) 213-9382 anytime to test a virtual agent. Schedule a personalized demo today to learn how to implement virtual agents and improve your business.

text:
Before Laurel
As the top-ranked law firm for tech innovators and investors, speed and client trust are competitive differentiators. The organization needed a timekeeping solution that was as far ahead of the curve as its attorneys and clients.
After Laurel
Time Automation greatly accelerated the pace of timekeeping, with a 40% increase in release velocity. A 24% increase in the number of tasks captured ensured bills were more precise, improving client trust, and 70% of users releasing more billable time significantly lifted firm revenue.
How valuable is Laurel? We asked the firm’s timekeepers
An investor puts their money on a promising young entrepreneur. A company takes the strategic step of acquiring a competitor. A private equity f irm backs a bold and innovative new brand. These types of deals tend to be featured in the business headlines, but just as fast-paced and fascinating are the law firms working tirelessly behind the scenes to guarantee that all goes according to plan.
And no one does that better than this international firm. Trusted by first-time startups, emerging and established businesses, and the investors that back them, the firm has been ranked as the top of its class by PitchBook for the last eight years. One of the keys to its success? Hiring the best lawyers in the industry, and empowering them with tools and processes that are as cutting-edge as their clients.
Every technology investment the organization makes benefits individual attorneys and the business as a whole—and for the firm, timekeeping was the next frontier. It was essential to find a solution that would enable its lawyers to keep pace with the breakneck speed of the innovation economy without burning out.
For years, firm managers had been observing how their conventional time capture tool was leaking billable time and encountering poor adoption. So when they came across Time Automation that shifts the timekeeping paradigm from lawyers telling a machine what they did during their workday to the machine telling the lawyers, they knew it was the right choice. That’s why the firm chose to roll out Laurel.
Time capture just can’t cut it
Lawyers despise time capture. It provides them with a seemingly bottomless pile of disorganized time entries that they then have to painstakingly categorize and correct before release—meaning they spend their time on mind-numbing busywork when they could’ve spent it on work that actually matters.
The firm ushered in Laurel to free its lawyers from draining administrative tasks, boost their happiness and productivity, and directly impact the bottom line. Laurel’s AI-powered automation runs unobtrusively in the background, capturing all of a lawyer’s billable activities, intelligently assigning them to the correct Client Matters and work codes, and formatting them as a review-ready timesheet.
How much better was Laurel? The team did a head-to-head comparison with Intapp Time, monitoring time released, the number and granularity of time entries, and the speed at which entries were released into the billing system.
More time captured and more time released means higher revenue
Because Time Automation is so effective in tracking activity across a firm’s chosen apps, websites, document management software, and phone systems, 70% of users reported that they were able to capture and release more time.
Similar to other firms that have deployed Laurel, timekeepers were often capturing an extra 30–60 minutes every day, and a few attorneys reported even more. If these gains were extended across the entire firm, they could equate to over $100,000 every single day—and tens of millions each year.
Each timekeeper also increased the number of time entries they released into the billing system. Laurel prevented time leakage by capturing all digital work activity across emails, documents, research sites, phone calls, calendar meetings, and other work applications, and as a result, timesheet granularity rose by an average of 24%.
AI, the driving force behind Time Automation, predicts Client Matters and Phase Task codes and links related sessions and tasks. All timekeepers need to do is to make final edits to their timesheets before releasing them into the billing system. This proved to be a huge benefit to the firm, since greater precision improves client trust in bills and improves realization rates.
The speed of release, from the time the work is performed to the time it enters the billing system, increased as well. Release velocity with Laurel was more than 40% faster than it was with Intapp Time—again, because the timesheets created by Laurel are review-ready with all entries properly categorized. This allows timekeepers to get hours into the billing system faster, ensures work is billed to the client in a timely manner, and shortens the collection cycle.
“As someone who struggles to enter my time when things get crazy busy, Laurel was able to capture the universe of emails, calls, etc. without my having to reverse engineer where I spent my time.” - Corporate Associate
A strong vote of confidence for Laurel
The benefits of Time Automation were immediate and tangible. It didn’t take long for the firm’s lawyers to get used to the software, with more than half feeling fully accustomed to it in five days or less. In the first two weeks, 80% of users also saw the system’s accuracy improve, since Laurel’s machine learning models learn from behavior and become more refined with increased use. This demonstrates that over the longer term, timekeeping will get even easier.
“Laurel captures more time for computer-based tasks, as it is far more diligent than I could be about recording each email, document view, etc.” - Litigation Associate
In the end, Intapp Time couldn’t compete with Laurel—over 90% of timekeepers agreed that adopting Laurel would be key to moving the firm closer to a successful daily time release policy. Now, the firm is a delighted customer, and has made Laurel the default timekeeping tool that their new associates learn as soon as they’re welcomed to the team.

text:
VIEW SURVEY RESULTS ONLINE AT EPA.GOV/CWNS
2022 Clean Watersheds Needs Survey
ABOUT THE CWNS
The Clean Watersheds Needs Survey compiles data on existing clean
water infrastructure and the need for future investment to address the
water quality objectives of the Clean Water Act (CWA) over the next
20 years. As directed by Congress, the U.S. Environmental Protection
Agency (EPA) collected needs and technical data for projects eligible for
Clean Water State Revolving Fund loans. These data show a nationwide
picture of clean water infrastructure across four categories: wastewater,
stormwater, decentralized wastewater treatment, and nonpoint source
control.
All U.S. states and territories participated in this voluntary survey,
marking the first time in the survey’s history that it has achieved 100
percent participation.
NATIONAL AND STATE NEEDS
The total nationwide reported needs are $630.1 billion as of January 1,
2022. Figure 1 displays the geographic distribution of the total reported
needs by state. Six states - New York, California, Florida, Virginia,
Louisiana, and Georgia - accounted for 42 percent of the nationwide
needs. On a per capita basis, the Northern Mariana Islands ($7,203),
West Virginia ($6,182), and New Mexico ($5,799) have the three highest
needs.
NEEDS
Refers to an unfunded project (or portion
of a project) and the associated capital
cost that addresses a water quality
or water-quality-related public health
problem existing as of January 1, 2022, or
that is expected to occur within the next
20 years.
TECHNICAL DATA
Refers to non-cost related data. For
example: wastewater or stormwater flow;
population served; and descriptive data
on discharge, effluent, unit processes, and
utility management.
Figure 1. Distribution of total reported needs by state (January 2022 dollars in billions).

EPA Publication Number: 832F24005
WASTEWATER
$345.7 Billion
55% of Total
Slightly over 40% of
reported wastewater needs
are for installing new or
repairing existing pipes and
pump stations.
STORMWATER
$115.3 Billion
18% of Total
Roughly $33.0 billion of the
stormwater total are for
nutrient reductions in the
Chesapeake Bay watershed.
NONPOINT
SOURCE CONTROL
$94.4 Billion
15% of Total
55% of the NPS control
needs are reported by six
states.
DECENTRALIZED
$74.7 Billion
12% of Total
43 states reported
decentralized needs,
including needs for both
individual onsite septic
systems and clustered
systems.
NATIONAL WASTEWATER TREATMENT TRENDS
In addition to collecting data on capital investments, the CWNS tracks trends in wastewater treatment for the U.S.
population. As of January 2022, there are 17,544 publicly owned treatment works (POTW) serving 270.4 million
Americans, or 82 percent of the population. The wastewater industry has seen significant improvements in treatment
since 1972: the number of people living in the U.S. served by POTWs with advanced treatment increased from less than 4
percent in 1972 to about 42 percent in 2022. The U.S. population served by systems with less-than-secondary treatment
decreased from almost 28 percent to an estimated 1 percent (Figure 2).
LOOKING FORWARD
Although the 2022 CWNS represents the
most comprehensive report on clean water
infrastructure needs in the United States, the
reported $630.1 billion likely underestimates
the true nationwide need for clean water
infrastructure investments for many reasons,
including:
• The CWNS encompasses a 20-year
planning horizon, but most planning
documents are designed for 5-10 years.
• The last CWNS occurred in 2012, which
meant many states had to reestablish
connections and conduct significantly
more outreach to prepare for the 2022
survey.
• The CWNS does not include Tribal
wastewater needs, which are documented by a separate survey conducted by the Indian Health Service.
Unprecedented funding from the 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act has provided much needed investment
in communities’ water infrastructure. It is important to note that projects included in the CWNS may already be part
of a municipality’s funding plans, even if funding has not been committed, and inclusion in the survey should not be
interpreted as a request for additional federal funding.
Maintaining the data collection cycle and full participation in the survey are crucial to ensuring that investment
opportunities are not overlooked, particularly in historically underserved communities and communities that are facing
impacts due to climate change.EPA remains committed to continually improving the CWNS and working collaboratively
across the clean water sector to achieve a more sustainable future.
Visit www.epa.gov/cwns for more information on the CWNS including the full report and 2022 CWNS Data Dashboard,
which features interactive maps, charts, and data tables at the national, state, and facility level.

Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions (NRES) is an incentive program that can help you offset the cost of the electricity you buy from Eversource with the energy you generate with non-residential solar or other Connecticut Class I renewable technologies.
This program replaced the Low and Zero Emission Renewable Energy Credit Program.
If you have questions about the NRES Program at Eversource, visit our solar help center to view frequently asked questions. For further guidance, please email ctcommrenewables@eversource.com or call 844-726-7573.
The year 5 procurement process was developed via Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA) Docket No. 25-08-03.
In program years 2 and beyond, there will be two opportunities to submit an NRES bid, tentatively scheduled for February and August each year.

The program year 5 (2026) August request for proposals (RFP) will open at 1 p.m. EPT on August 3, 2026.

The RFP process is determined by the size of the project.
The Small Zero Emission project selection process is as follows: (1) if capacity is reached via bids submitted during the two-week window, selection is based on a lottery, and (2) if capacity is not reached during the two-week window, all eligible projects submitted during the window are selected, and subsequent to the window, eligible projects are selected on a rolling, first-come first-served basis.
Projects greater than 200kW up to and including 5,000kW are awarded tariff agreements through a competitive solicitation process. Bidding will take place in an online bid portal during the RFP window.
In Year 5, we will award projects in the Small Zero, Medium Zero, and Large Zero Emission categories until a budgetary or a MW cap is reached, whichever occurs first. The School Solar will operate with only a MW cap.

A REC is generated for each megawatt-hour (MWh) of electricity that your system generates regardless of whether you use the energy or it is exported to the electric grid.
Before submitting a bid, the Customer of Record must pick from two incentive compensation options: Buy-All or Netting. Each is designed to provide a similar return on investment. For current incentive rates, please see the current RFP document in the RFP Information section.
With the Buy-All Incentive, you will export all power that your system produces to the electric grid without first suppling power to your building.
- We will purchase power from you at a rate approved by the Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA)
- You'll receive compensation as either an on-bill credit to offset your monthly bill or a cash payment once per quarter. You may specify a percentage of your compensation to be split between the two options
- You will purchase the electricity you need to power your building directly from Eversource
- Any on-bill credits not used to offset your bill can be cashed out at the end of the 20-year term
- Any cash payments can go to a third party, called a Tariff Payment Beneficiary
With the Buy-All Incentive, your power generation and consumption are measured using separate meters installed at your building.
With the Netting Incentive, you'll first supply power from the system to your building and only export excess power to the electric grid.
- Power produced by your system, but not consumed within the month, is "netted" at the same rate you pay Eversource for electricity
- Net credits are applied to your bill in dollars and will be used to offset future customer, supply and delivery charges
- Any excess credits can be carried over each month and cashed out if you stop electric service
- Once enrolled, your compensation rate (in dollars per kilowatt hour) for net production will fluctuate with the prevailing retail rate over a 20-year term
With the Netting Incentive, you’ll receive a new meter that measures how much energy you consume and how much is exported to the grid. You'll also receive a second meter to measure the energy produced by your project.
State, Agricultural or Municipal (SAM) customers have the opportunity to share compensation from renewable energy generation with other SAM customers. Both the Buy-All and Netting incentives are available.
SAM projects must identify the initial beneficial accounts when a bid is submitted by using the Beneficial Account Credit Allocation Form found in the Forms section below.
Just as with the standard Buy-All incentive, if you're a SAM customer who chooses the Buy-All Incentive, you'll:
- Receive compensation for all of the energy you generate
- Separately purchase the electricity you need to power your building from Eversource
As a SAM customer, you can choose to assign a percentage of your total compensation to other SAM accounts such as a public school, police department or public works department.
With this option, you net credits the same way as the standard Netting Incentive. You'll:
- First use the energy you generate with your system
- Receive credits for any excess generation (in dollars) at the same rate you pay Eversource for electricity
As a SAM customer, you can apply a percentage of your excess credits to other SAM accounts. You'll choose what percentage of your excess power generation value to apply to other SAM beneficial accounts.

When Matt Buckwalter bought out his partner and became the majority owner of Punctual Pros in 2021, he made his intentions clear: He wanted to bring the company to market.
Buckwalter’s plan became a reality recently when he sold Punctual Pros’ territories in central Pennsylvania to Broad Sky Partners for an undisclosed amount. His company’s portfolio consists of three home service franchises under Authority Brands: One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, Benjamin Franklin Plumbing and Mister Sparky.
The deal gives Broad Sky Partners, a middle market private equity firm based in New York City, majority ownership of the first tri-brand operator under Authority Brands.
Punctual Pros is one of the platform company’s largest franchisees in terms of the number of zip codes it covers. The four brick-and-mortar franchise locations and one satellite location that Punctual Pros own provide home services for 240 zip code territories in central Pennsylvania.
Apax Partners-backed Authority Brands has 229 units of One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning, Benjamin Franklin Plumbing and Mister Sparky covering more than 820 zip codes.
In December 2022, Authority Brands acquired The Junkluggers in a 100 percent buyout transaction to bring its growing platform to 16 home services brands. The company has more than 1,900 franchise locations.
As part of deal, Buckwalter agreed to stay on as CEO of his Lancaster, Pennsylvania-based company and retain his executive team. He said his main responsibility will be identifying independent home service providers for potential acquisitions to bolster growth in the Mid-Atlantic states. He said he’s targeting potential businesses in Maryland and possibly New Jersey in the near term.
“We had a lot of interest from other firms in buying us, and we ended up whittling it down to eight finalists,” said Buckwalter. “With Broad Sky as a financial partner, we feel confident that we can become the absolute dominate player in plumbing, heating, air conditioning and electric services.”
Buckwalter said Punctual Pros, founded in 1958 as The Rohrer Company, nearly tripled its business in the last five years.
“We were attracted to the strength of leaders Matt Buckwalter and Aaron Buckwalter who, along with their team, have driven key operational metrics and cultivated a values-driven, people-first culture,” Jonathan Marlow, partner at Broad Sky Partners, said in a statement.
With Broad Sky’s marketing and franchising support, Buckwalter said Punctual Pros could even quadruple its unit count in the next three to five years. Punctual Pros is the private equity firm’s first venture in the home service category and first investment in franchise brands.
“They have very skilled people around marketing, around operations and HR related issues to help streamline some of the things we do and help alleviate the growing pains, so to speak,” Buckwalter said.

BV Investment Partners Announces Recapitalization of Intelliteach
BOSTON, February 1, 2019 – BV Investment Partners (“BV”), a middle-market private equity firm focused on the business services, software and IT services sectors, today announced that it has partnered with management to acquire Intelliteach, a leading, global provider of tech enabled, business process outsourcing solutions for law and accounting firms, from Dominus Capital, L.P. Intelliteach is the seventh investment in BV’s ninth fund, which has $750 million of committed capital.
Headquartered in St. Louis, with offices in Atlanta, London, Toronto, and Goa (India), Intelliteach serves over 300 law and accounting firms globally. The Company specializes in “white glove” IT help desk support, IT Managed Services (Development, Infrastructure, Engineering and Legacy Software Support), Managed Financial Services (e-billing processing, accounts receivable management, and cash application) and training and education through its e-learning platform. Its managed IT and financial offerings are augmented with proprietary software platforms that support a data driven service delivery model. Intelliteach’s clients on average have experienced a 10X return on their investment and/or reduced overall operating expense by more than 30%, all while improving quality of service which is available 24/7, 365 days a year.
Seelin Naidoo, Chief Executive Officer of Intelliteach, said, “for over 20 years Intelliteach has served as a trusted, long-term partner for its clients, helping law and accounting firms solve their complex IT and financial services challenges. With BV’s assistance we intend to build upon Intelliteach’s strong foundation to continue to enhance our current service offerings while developing additional services that will deliver enhanced value to our customers and employees. The market for our outsourced technology and business processes is still vastly underpenetrated, so we are excited to begin our next chapter with BV.”
Matt Kinsey, Managing Director of BV, said, “Intelliteach has positioned itself as a trusted adviser through its technology enabled service offerings. Seelin and his team have built a business that delivers unique value to its customers, and we’re thrilled to be backing them in the recapitalization of the business. We’re looking forward to supporting the team’s growth strategy in any way we can, and believe our deep industry experience base and network can be applied to help Intelliteach continue to scale organically as well as through acquisitions.”
In connection with the investment, Mike Bryant, an industry expert and current Chairman of legal process outsourcing business, HaystackID, will join the board of directors. Mr. Bryant has a long track record of success in the legal outsourcing market and will provide strategic guidance and support with various growth initiatives.
“We are investing in a business with exceptional fundamentals, supported by long-term industry tailwinds, and backed by a management team in which we have great conviction.” said Jason Kustka, Principal of BV. “We think that Intellitech is only at the beginning stages of its evolution and look forward to helping management take advantage of an attractive market opportunity.”
About Intelliteach
Intelliteach is the leading global provider of intelligent outsourcing solutions to more than 300 firms in the legal and accounting markets. With focus on providing secure, scalable solutions enabled by best in class technology platforms, our multi service solutions help to position law firms for financial success by allowing them to emphasize long-term practice growth strategies and transformative law practices. See what’s next with Intelliteach at www.INTELLITEACH.com.

BV Investment Partners is currently investing its ninth private equity fund. The firm is one of the oldest and most experienced sector-focused private equity firms in North America. Since its founding in 1983, the firm has invested over $3.4 billion, actively targeting investments in the business services, software and IT services industries. Consumers Expected to Return Nearly $850 Billion in Merchandise in 2025
“Retailers are constantly evolving and working to meet customer expectations, and they recognize the importance the returns process plays.”
WASHINGTON – Retailers estimate that 15.8% of their annual sales will be returned this year, totaling $849.9 billion, according to the 2025 Retail Returns Landscape report released today by the National Retail Federation and Happy Returns, a UPS company. The returns rate is in line with 16.9% last year, when returns totaled $890 billion.
“Returns are no longer the end point of a transaction,” NRF Vice President of Industry and Consumer Insights Katherine Cullen said. “They provide an opportunity for retailers to create a positive experience for customers and can translate to brand loyalty. Retailers are constantly evolving and working to meet customer expectations, and they recognize the importance the returns process plays.”
While overall return rates may remain steady, some areas are facing more pressure than others. According to the report, an estimated 19.3% of online sales will be returned in 2025.
Additionally, as Gen Z’s influence grows, so does their impact on returns. Those between the ages of 18 and 30 made 7.7 returns of online purchases in the last 12 months, on average, more than any other generation.
Consumer expectations are increasing around returns. Free returns are a major draw for shoppers, with 82% citing them as a major consideration when making a purchase, up from 76% last year. Consumers also value immediacy, with 76% saying they are more likely to choose a return option that provides an instant refund or exchange.
Still, a poor returns experience can deter future purchases. About 71% of consumers say they are less likely to shop with a retailer again after a poor experience, up from 67% in 2024. And four out of five said they will share their negative experience with friends and family, potentially amplifying the impact.
Retailers are faced with balancing customer expectations and the need to grow online channels against the rising operational costs associated with returns as well as pressures from external factors like tariffs. Retailers surveyed indicate their top priorities for 2026 are increasing online sales and reducing return rates. The top reasons retailers charge for returns are increases in the cost of operations to process returns (40%), increases in carrier shipping costs (40%) and economic uncertainty and risk of tariffs (33%). Overall, nearly two-thirds (64%) of merchants say updating their returns process in the next six months is a priority.
Return fraud is an ongoing concern for the industry. The report found that 9% of all returns are fraudulent. Retailers that track such incidents noted increases in practices like overstated quantity of returns (71%), empty box or “box of rocks” (65%) and decoy returns such as counterfeit items (64%). Technology offers partial relief, with artificial intelligence being a popular option — 85% said they are employing AI to detect or prevent return fraud.
Meanwhile consumers, especially younger consumers, continue to make returns choices that are costly to retailers. Close to two-thirds of consumers admit to participating in at least one costly returns behavior, from wardrobing and “bracketing” to sending back different items or empty boxes. Just under half (45%) believe “bending the truth” is acceptable when making returns, especially if they are unsatisfied with their purchase.
“Return policies and their overall process have transformed into a strategic touchpoint for retailers, influencing how younger consumers shop from the outset,” said David Sobie, co-founder and CEO of Happy Returns. “To stay competitive amid rising return rates and behaviors like bracketing, retailers must modernize their reverse logistics to enhance customer satisfaction, reduce fraud and safeguard their operations in today’s high-pressure retail landscape.”
Ahead of the winter holiday season, the report also found that retailers expect 17% of holiday sales to be returned, consistent with previous years. Retailers plan to manage holiday returns and fraudulent activity by increasing focus on third-party logistics partners (49%), hiring seasonal staff to handle returns (43%) and extending return windows (37%).
About the Survey
NRF and Happy Returns, a UPS company, conducted two surveys this summer to understand the dynamics of online returns from both consumers and ecommerce professionals. The first survey included responses from 2,006 consumers who had returned at least one online purchase within the past 12 months, exploring their shopping preferences, return experiences and expectations for the upcoming 2025 winter holiday season. The second survey engaged 358 professionals involved in ecommerce for large (over $500 million in revenue) U.S. merchants representing a mix of verticals to gather insights into their return rates and operational challenges associated with returns processing.
View the 2025 Retail Returns Landscape report here.
As the leading authority and voice for the retail industry, NRF conducts research throughout the year, staying on the pulse of the industry and consumer behavior as they evolve.
About NRF
The National Retail Federation passionately advocates for the people, brands, policies and ideas that help retail succeed. From its headquarters in Washington, D.C., NRF empowers the industry that powers the economy. Retail is the nation’s largest private-sector employer, contributing $5.3 trillion to annual GDP and supporting more than one in four U.S. jobs — 55 million working Americans. For over a century, NRF has been a voice for every retailer and every retail job, educating, inspiring and communicating the powerful impact retail has on local communities and global economies. nrf.com
About Happy Returns
Happy Returns, a UPS company, provides end-to-end returns solutions for online retailers and shoppers through a unique combination of returns software plus reverse logistics. Through its nationwide network of Return Bar® locations, Happy Returns delights shoppers by enabling them to drop off returns with no packaging or printing in under 60 seconds. Returns are consolidated, sorted in automated facilities, and bulk shipped back to retailers, improving operational efficiency and helping prevent fraud through item-level verification. Managing Partner's Messages
- Managing Partner
Thankful for our Clients, Colleagues, and Friends
All,
As we celebrate Thanksgiving, I am reminded of how much we have to be grateful for—not only during this season but every day! Earlier this year, we marked our 30th anniversary, and reflecting on that milestone fills me with pride and appreciation. From a three-attorney boutique to a full-service firm of nearly 90 attorneys across five offices in four states, our journey has been nothing short of remarkable! I am proud of who we have become and so appreciative of each and every one of our employees – all of whom share the Firm’s objective to set the gold standard for what a law firm can and should be.
First and foremost, thank you to our clients for placing your trust in us with your most sensitive and important matters. That trust is the foundation of everything we do. We approach your issues as if they were our own, committed to delivering solutions with the same care, urgency, and cost-effectiveness we would for our own family or business.
I am equally thankful for our extraordinary team, whose passion, dedication, and sense of purpose have shaped a culture that is vibrant, inclusive, and deeply committed to professional excellence and giving back. This year, that commitment was recognized in meaningful ways:
- Chambers USA 2025 ranked three of our practice areas and twelve of our attorneys, affirming our reputation for excellence in Commercial Litigation, White Collar Crime & Investigations, and Bankruptcy & Restructuring.
- The New Jersey Law Journal named our firm Appellate Department of the Year for eight years running —a testament to the skill and dedication of our appellate team—and named us a finalist for Law Firm of the Year for three years in a row (having been named winner in 2023).
These accolades are more than honors; they are proof that our vision works—combining best-in-class legal services with a culture of purpose and integrity.
Through the Justice Gary S. Stein Public Interest Center, we continue to lead by example, demonstrating that a law firm can thrive while advancing justice. Our attorneys have devoted thousands of pro bono hours to landmark cases involving constitutional rights, government transparency, defense of democracy and the rule of law, and social and economic justice. This work gives meaning to what we do and reflects our belief that lawyers have a responsibility to effect real change.
As we look ahead, we remain steadfast in our mission: to advocate tenaciously for our clients – to do whatever is necessary to advance their interests -- and to continue building a firm where a foundational sense of meaning and purpose fuels the passion necessary to consistently deliver the top shelf legal work that our clients have come to expect and that we demand.
On behalf of all of us at Pashman Stein, I wish you and your loved ones a Thanksgiving filled with warmth, peace, and gratitude.
With appreciation,
Managing Partner
Celebrating 30 Years of Excellence and Continuing to Raise the Bar!
* * * * * *

Celebrating 30 Years of Excellence and Continuing to Raise the Bar!
Today, July 1, marks the 30th anniversary of the founding of Pashman Stein. It has been an exciting and remarkable journey, and I couldn’t be more proud of the firm that we have become. We have evolved from a 3-attorney litigation boutique into a full-service law firm of nearly 90 attorneys with 5 offices across New Jersey, New York, Delaware, and Pennsylvania. As I take a moment to reflect back on the last 30 years, I am thankful for each of our clients - for trusting us with their most sensitive and important legal and business issues, knowing that we approach their issues as if they were our own – and for our peers, colleagues, family, and friends who have been an integral part of our success.
The goal in starting our own firm was to bring together exceptional attorneys who provide best-in-class legal services with the utmost professional excellence who also share a sense of purpose in giving back and tackling the important public interest issues of our day. A firm where maintaining work-life balance and a vibrant and inclusive culture informs every decision we make.
In what could be considered a proof-of-concept moment, last year the New Jersey Law Journal named our firm its 2023 “Law Firm of the Year,” due in part to the firm’s excellence in litigation and appellate work, as well as to the firm’s Justice Gary S. Stein Public Interest Center, through which our attorneys continue to provide pro bono legal services and litigate impactful legal issues in areas including constitutional law, government transparency, social and economic justice, and criminal justice. That recognition offered tangible evidence that we could engage in public policy litigation and be part of the important policy debates of our time and that such impactful work could fully align with our business imperatives.
At Pashman Stein, we believe in tenaciously advocating for our clients and in defending the Constitution and the rule of law. That is why earlier this year, as one of only seven New Jersey-headquartered law firms to do so (and the only major New Jersey-headquartered firm), Pashman Stein signed the Munger, Tolles & Olson/Eimer Stahl amicus brief filed April 2025 in the lawsuit challenging the Executive Orders issued against Perkins Coie. In addition, Pashman Stein signed the amicus brief filed in each of the lawsuits challenging the Executive Orders Issued against WilmerHale, Jenner & Block, and Susman Godfrey. I am incredibly proud that we were willing to stand up for our convictions and the rule of law, notwithstanding the risks and not knowing which other firms were joining.
Given our emphasis on professional excellence, we value the feedback of our clients and the attorneys with whom we work, whether as co-counsel or opposing counsel. That is why we take great pride in the recently released rankings by Chambers and Partners, which are widely considered to be the gold standard of legal rankings and are based on independent research, reputation in the market, and feedback from clients and peer attorneys.
In the Chambers 2025 USA Guide, Pashman Stein has 3 ranked practice areas and 12 ranked attorneys -- Commercial Litigation (Mike Stein, Brendan Walsh, and Dan Guadalupe), White Collar Crime & Investigations (Joe Hayden, Justin Walder, Aidan O’Connor, and Remi Spencer), and Bankruptcy, Restructuring & Creditors’ Rights (John Weiss, Joe Barsalona, Henry Jaffe, and David Stratton) – as well as a ranking for attorney Seth Goldberg.
As our reputation continues to attract many attorneys who previously worked at large, international law firms, we pride ourselves in being able to provide the same top-notch representation at a more cost-effective rate structure.
With the future holding many exciting possibilities, we look forward to continuing our measured growth and the expansion of our practice areas to meet our clients’ needs, while never losing sight of the principles upon which the firm was founded.
Cheers to 30 Years!

Reflections on the New Jersey Law Journal's 2024 Legal Awards
I am thrilled to share that the New Jersey Law Journal has recognized our firm and attorneys in 8 categories as part of its 2024 New Jersey Legal Awards! During the nearly 30 years that Pashman Stein has been in business, we have worked hard to earn our reputation for excellence and commitment to our clients’ causes. The recognition by the New Jersey Law Journal in so many categories year after year provides, I believe, tangible evidence that our hard work is paying off!
With congratulations to each and every one of our employees, I am honored to report that our firm won in the following categories:
- Appellate Department of the Year. This is the sixth time in seven years that we have won this award. (The award was not given to any firm last year; we were named winner of the broader category of 2023 Law Firm of the Year.) This award reflects the outstanding work of our appellate attorneys on commercial cases and, under the leadership of director CJ Griffin, on pro bono and public interest matters through the Justice Gary S. Stein Public Interest Center.
- Dealmakers Award for our Bankruptcy Group. Given New Jersey’s prominence as a go-to venue for bankruptcy filings, it is an honor for our bankruptcy practice group to be recognized by the New Jersey Law Journal as the winner of the 2024 Dealmakers award. In just over two years, our Bankruptcy, Restructuring & Creditors’ Rights practice, under the leadership of chair John W. Weiss, has experienced unprecedented growth, exceeding expectations and providing exceptional value to clients by offering top-notch legal services at a more cost-effective rate structure.
- Lifetime Achievement Award for Justin Walder. This is a well-deserved award recognizing the long and illustrious career of Justin P. Walder. We are fortunate to call Justin our partner, as he is one of the finest lawyers I know and whose reputation for professional excellence is legendary!
In addition, we also were named a finalist in the following categories:
- Law Firm of the Year (Last year, the firm was named the winner of the 2023 Law Firm of the Year award.)
- Litigation Department of the Year (This is the second year in a row that the firm has been named a finalist for Litigation Department of the Year-General.)
- Cannabis Law Firm of the Year
Watching Pashman Stein grow and thrive over the years, while earning a reputation for professional excellence, has been a source of great pride to me and to everyone who works at the firm. I look forward to embracing the endless possibilities that lie ahead and to continually adapting to best serve our clients’ needs.

Reflections on Our Ranking in Chambers USA Guide 2024
I am thrilled to share the news that Chambers USA Guide 2024 has ranked the firm in New Jersey in Litigation: General Commercial for the 9th year in a row and in Litigation: White-Collar Crime & Government Investigations for the 21st year in a row! In addition, six of the firm’s attorneys are ranked in the 2024 Chambers USA Guide: Daniel R. Guadalupe, Joseph A. Hayden, Jr., Aidan P. O’Connor, Justin P. Walder, Henry J. Jaffe, and me.
The honor is especially gratifying in light of our having been named Law Firm of the Year by the New Jersey Law Journal last fall as part of its 2023 New Jersey Legal Awards.
Commercial Litigation
In recognition of the excellence and commitment of the firm’s attorneys, our firm’s Commercial Litigation department was elevated to Band 2 for New Jersey in the 2024 Chambers USA Guide. In addition to my own Band 2 ranking in Commercial Litigation, our partner Daniel R. Guadalupe is now Chambers-ranked.
We are very proud that we have received this prestigious ranking, and that the department has been elevated to Band 2 for General Commercial Litigation in New Jersey. Led by co-chairs, Sean Mack and Brendan M. Walsh, our attorneys are go-to litigators for complex litigation because of their experience, work ethic, and knowledge of local judicial culture. Because of the depth and strength of the firm’s litigation group, we also are regularly retained as local counsel by national and international corporations of all sizes and by major, multinational Am Law 100 firms.
Criminal Defense & Governmental Investigations
The firm’s Criminal Defense & Government Investigations practice is ranked in Band 2 for New Jersey in the 2024 Chambers USA Guide, representing the 21st year the practice has been ranked by Chambers – longer than any other ranked practice in this category for which information is available! The practice is led by co-chairs, Joseph A. Hayden, Jr., who has been Chambers-ranked for 22 years and continues to maintain his Chambers Band 1 ranking, and Aidan P. O’Connor, who has been Chambers-ranked for 12 years and continues to maintain his Chambers Band 2 ranking. Partner Justin P. Walder, who has been Chambers-ranked for 22 years, is also ranked as Senior Statesman in this category.
Our well-earned reputation for professional excellence throughout the region is reflected in these long-running Chambers rankings of our attorneys. We take great pride in our team’s commitment to vigorously defending our clients’ interests, which includes implementing strategies to avoid criminal prosecution.
Bankruptcy, Restructuring & Creditor's Rights
In addition, I am pleased to announce that Henry J. Jaffe, partner in the firm’s Bankruptcy, Restructuring & Creditors’ Rights practice, has been ranked in the 2024 Chambers USA Guide in Delaware, representing the 9th year that Henry has been ranked by Chambers.
Henry was added to the firm’s growing roster of bankruptcy attorneys from AmLaw 100 firms and Chambers ranked-bankruptcy practices last year, joining chair John W. Weiss, who established the practice in March 2022, and partner Joseph C. Barsalona II, who joined the group shortly thereafter. Together, they represent clients throughout the country, with a well-deserved reputation for high-caliber representation and innovative solutions at a cost-effective rate structure.
Having a Chambers-ranked lawyer of Henry’s caliber and reputation continues to elevate the outstanding client service and reputation for which our bankruptcy practice is known.
