Narrative: Across 34 cases from 1996 to 2026, the highest-value exits did the same six things in roughly the same order; Punctual Pros is about 30 months into its own version. First, the sponsor put an operator team in charge at entry: Alpine named Apex's CEO and CFO on launch day in July 2019 with $100M+ of committed equity, American Capital gave Service Experts' returning CEO about 10% ownership, and Huron recruited Sciens' CEO before it bought its first company. Second, the first add-on came early and close to home, a median of about 7 months after entry across 11 dated cases, as Smith + Howard did with Market Street Partners in month 9 and Punctual Pros did with Horvath in month 8. Third, the tuck-ins kept coming at roughly one every three to five months: Trivest did 16 at TurnPoint while revenue grew nearly 10x, Huron did 13 at Sciens while revenue and EBITDA rose more than 35x, and BSP did nine at Smith + Howard while headcount went from about 100 to about 800. Fourth, every brand ran on one system: CenterOak ran a single IT system and consolidated purchasing at Service Champions, Wrench now books online at 99% of its locations on ServiceTitan, and Authority Brands moved Punctual Pros and every other One Hour, Benjamin Franklin and Mister Sparky location onto ServiceTitan in September 2024. Fifth, they built recurring revenue that buyers pay for: Champions grew from about 60,000 members in 2021 to about 150,000 in 2026 (about 71 to 83 per technician) and sold to Blackstone in February 2026 at a reported ~18.5x trailing EBITDA, while Frontdoor gets 76% of its revenue from renewals with 84% of customers on auto-pay. Sixth, they owned the technician pipeline: Champions more than doubled its field technicians from 850 to 1,800+, Shermco grew certified technicians from 400+ to 600+ as Gryphon doubled revenue and sold for about $1.6B, and Sila bought a trade school in January 2026. Margin beat volume in the best compounders, as VWR grew Adjusted EBITDA 8.6% a year against 3.7% sales growth from 2006 to 2013 and IES grew operating income 88% on 21% more revenue in FY2024. In the last 12-18 months before a sale the winners kept buying and published KPIs: Shermco closed five add-ons in the 17 months before Blackstone, Sila added four brands in the nine months before Goldman's ~$1.7B (~17x) purchase, and Smith + Howard disclosed more than 600 employees and ~$175M of expected revenue about five months before TPG signed. Most exits went to a larger sponsor, often with the seller or management rolling equity (Charlesbank into GI Partners at ARS, Odyssey alongside Blackstone at Champions, BV alongside BSP at Frontline), and the median first-sponsor hold was about 4.4 years (4.0 in residential home services). The failures show what not to copy: Any Hour signed 16 partnerships in about 13 months and its loan now carries PIK at ~89% of par, TurnPoint grew from 17 to 65 brands and now pays PIK under a new CEO, Horizon is lender-supported, and Roto-Rooter's parent Chemed raised ad spend about $11M from 2023 to 2025 while segment revenue fell about $50M. For Punctual Pros the order is an integration leader and a ServiceTitan KPI pack now, members per technician as the north-star metric, one contiguous tuck-in per quarter in PA, NJ, MD and DE, a Lancaster academy with Thaddeus Stevens, leverage near the 2.9-3.3x lower-middle-market norm, and an exit-ready KPI pack by about 2028.

text:
Kind: use_case
Company: pp
Name: After-hours emergency dispatcher (One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky / Horvath lines)
Direction: inbound
Trigger: Any call outside staffed hours (weekday 5pm-8am, weekends, holidays) to a brand tracking number.
Flow:
- Greets with the brand name and says it is the virtual assistant.
- Runs a safety screen first (gas smell, CO alarm, sparking, water near panel) and gives 911/utility instructions when triggered.
- Matches caller ID to the ServiceTitan customer and confirms address and equipment on file.
- Classifies the job (no heat, no cool, active leak, no power) and priority (infant/elderly, freezing temps, NWS warning active).
- Checks on-call technician capacity and offers the earliest arrival window.
- States that an after-hours diagnostic fee applies and texts the amount and terms.
- Books the job on the dispatch board, pages the on-call tech, and texts the customer a confirmation and on-my-way link.
- Writes transcript, summary and disposition to the job record.
Handoff rule: Transfer to the on-call manager when there is a safety hazard the caller cannot leave, a commercial account, a complaint or billing dispute, the caller asks for a person twice, or two failed intent attempts; target live pickup within 60s, otherwise callback promise within 10 minutes.
Kpis:
after-hours answer rate; after-hours booking rate; time to book (s); abandon rate during greeting; jobs booked per on-call shift; escalation rate
Est annual value ($): 390,000
Value label: assumption
Value formula: 42,024 calls/yr x 0.12 after-hours x 0.35 lost x 0.8 recovered x 0.45 booked x 0.6 incremental x $1,024 = $390,000
Weeks to deploy: 3
Risk notes: Over-promising arrival times when on-call capacity is thin; must never diagnose safety issues; the quoted fee must match the franchise price book; brand guarantee wording (One Hour on-time promise) only where the window is honored.
Source url: https://www.servicetitan.com/features/pro/voice-agent

Kind: use_case
Company: pp
Name: Storm-day and lunch-hour overflow agent
Direction: inbound
Trigger: Call not answered by a CSR within 3 rings, queue depth above CSR count, or an NWS warning active for a PP forecast zone (the demand model's weather-response plans).
Flow:
- Answers on ring 3 with the brand greeting, virtual-assistant greeting and a one-line note that CSRs are on other calls.
- Captures the problem and safety screen; for storm calls asks about standing water, sump pump, power loss or surge damage.
- Confirms service area by zip (Punctual Pros ZIP coverage) and customer record.
- Applies storm triage rules (active water and no power first) and offers windows from live capacity.
- Books, adds job notes (e.g., water-heater check), and texts confirmation.
- Offers a callback from a CSR for non-urgent quotes so CSRs stay on emergencies.
Handoff rule: Hand to a CSR immediately when one frees up and the caller is mid-quote on a replacement, for commercial/property-manager accounts, or for any customer flagged VIP/complaint.
Kpis:
abandon rate; storm-day booked jobs; share of overflow booked; average speed of answer; CSR occupancy
Est annual value ($): 982,000
Value label: assumption
Value formula: 42,024 calls/yr x 0.88 daytime x 0.12 missed/abandoned x 0.8 x 0.45 x 0.6 x $1,024 = $982,000
Weeks to deploy: 3
Risk notes: Surge can exceed field capacity, so the agent must stop offering same-day slots when the board is full and offer a waitlist; storm messaging must not promise insurance outcomes.
Source url: https://www.servicetitan.com/toolbox/state-of-the-trades/trends/hvac-summer-after-hours-call-spike

Kind: use_case
Company: pp
Name: Outbound membership renewal and tune-up booking
Direction: outbound
Trigger: Membership renewal date within 30 days, or seasonal tune-up due (fall furnace / spring A/C), for members who asked for reminder calls.
Flow:
- Calls between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m. local time from the brand number, says it is the virtual assistant and asks if now is a good time.
- Answers 'is this a robot?' truthfully and offers a person at any point.
- Summarizes plan benefits and the member's history (last tune-up, discounts applied).
- Renews via card on file or a secure payment link (never reads card numbers aloud).
- Books the tune-up from live capacity.
- Texts confirmation and logs outcome; stops calling at once if the member asks.
Handoff rule: Transfer to a CSR for cancellations with complaints, price objections beyond the scripted response, or any request to speak to a person; failed payments go to a human queue.
Kpis:
renewal rate; tune-ups booked per 100 calls; opt-out rate; complaints per 1,000 calls; revenue per member
Est annual value ($): 403,000
Value label: assumption
Value formula: 6,000 members x (0.88 - 0.8) renewal lift x (fee $240 + member service revenue $600) = $403,000
Weeks to deploy: 4
Risk notes: A pushy renewal call costs a member; keep calls to members who asked for reminders and stop at once on request.
Source url: https://www.applausehq.com/blog/hvac-membership-programs

text:
Kind: architecture
Layer: pipeline
Name: Reference 24/7 dispatch call pipeline (cascaded)
Pipeline:
- Hop: telephony
What: Brand tracking number -> Twilio/SIP; brand greeting that names the virtual assistant; caller ID passed to the agent.
Budget ms: network/PSTN ~230 (mouth-to-ear 1,115 minus platform 885)
- Hop: streaming ASR + end-of-turn
What: Deepgram/AssemblyAI streaming with brand and township keyword boosting; semantic end-of-turn detection.
Budget ms: 350
Upper ms: 500
- Hop: LLM with tools
What: Claude (Messages API, streaming, strict tool schemas) decides the next utterance or tool call.
Budget ms: 375
Upper ms: 750
Tools:
customer_lookup(phone|address) -> ServiceTitan customer/location/equipment; check_capacity(zip, job_type, priority) -> open windows (Adaptive Capacity); book_job(customer_id, job_type, window, notes) -> job_id; send_payment_link(customer_id, amount_type) -> SMS link (no card data in voice); page_on_call(trade, priority, summary) -> acknowledgement; transfer_to_human(queue, summary) -> warm transfer; log_disposition(call_id, outcome, contact_preferences)
- Hop: TTS
What: Brand voice per franchise (ElevenLabs Flash or Cartesia Sonic), streamed sentence by sentence.
Budget ms: 100
Upper ms: 250
Latency budget:
Platform turn gap target ms: 885
Platform upper ms: 1100
Mouth to ear target ms: 1115
Mouth to ear upper ms: 1400
Human benchmark ms: 200
Tool call rule: Tool calls that exceed ~700 ms get a spoken filler ('Let me check the schedule...') so the turn gap never exceeds the 1.4 s upper limit.
Human handoff: Warm transfer with a spoken + written summary to the CSR queue (business hours) or on-call manager (after hours) on: safety hazard, explicit request for a person (second ask), two failed intents, payment dispute, VIP/commercial account, low ASR confidence on address after two tries. If no human answers within 60 s, the agent books a guaranteed callback and pages the manager.
Logging qa: Every call: recording, transcript, tool-call log, model/prompt version, disposition and greeting check. Score 100% of transcripts with an LLM rubric (safety screen asked, virtual-assistant introduction given, booking asked, correct fee wording) and have a human review a weighted 5% sample plus every escalation and complaint weekly.
Est cost per minute ($): 0.1158
Est cost breakdown per minute:
Telephony inbound: 0.0085
Recording: 0.0025
Asr deepgram nova3: 0.0048
Llm estimate: 0.03
Tts estimate: 0.02
Orchestration vapi: 0.05
Est cost note: Cascaded build ~$0.1158/min (LLM and TTS are estimates); a 4-minute call costs ~$0.46, vs $1.67-$3.00 per call for Smith.ai and $0.12-0.14/min all-in on Bland.

text:
Missed-call economics, vendors, use cases and guardrails

Generated: 2026-10-06
Portfolio company focus: pp
Method: Web research on 2026-10-06 (WebSearch/WebFetch) of vendor pricing pages, benchmark reports, case studies and funding coverage; figures were taken from the fetched page where possible (retrieval status 'fetched'), otherwise from the search-engine result for the cited URL ('search snippet'), or reused from sourced items already in this repo ('portal data': pp_ads.json, pp_nationwide.json, ai_agents_portfolio.json). The Punctual Pros revenue model is computed in code from pp_demand_model.json call baselines, pp_nationwide.json core housing units and the cited benchmarks; every use-case value is a labelled assumption with its formula.
Caveats:
- Vendor outcome numbers (booking rates, CSAT, deflection, ROI) are self-reported and unaudited; use them as ranges, not promises.
- Punctual Pros' actual call volume, missed-call rate, booking rate, membership count and tickets are not public; the model backs call volume out of the ~$22M revenue estimate and must be recalibrated from ServiceTitan data.
- Market call baselines (Punctual Pros demand model) are derived from homeowner surveys and are themselves estimates.
- Several benchmark pages were gated or not fetchable (Invoca report body, Azure pricing, PubMed HTML); items say so via retrieval status.
- Healthcare no-show evidence (Parikh 2010) is a proxy for home-service confirmations.
- Sample calls are illustrative scripts with fictional customers, addresses and technicians.
Thesis:
- Every unanswered call to a home-services company is a buyer with an urgent problem who will call the next number on Google, so phone coverage is a revenue line.
- Invoca's 2026 benchmark finds only 52% of home-services callers reach a person (65% of real calls over 15 seconds), and 55% of businesses never ask the caller to book.
- The leaks cluster exactly when demand peaks: ServiceTitan data show off-hours calls rise to 14% of HVAC inbound in June, and trades lose 30-40% of them.
- Speed decides who wins the job, because a lead called within 5 minutes is 21 times more likely to qualify than one called at 30 minutes (MIT/InsideSales), and the odds keep falling by the hour (HBR).
- AI voice agents now book at human-or-better rates: ServiceTitan reports 70% overall and 90% when capacity is open, versus a 42% typical human CSR booking rate.
- For Punctual Pros, a conservative model (about 3,502 inbound calls a month, 15% missed, 45% booked, 40% haircut for callers who would have called back) recovers about $1.4M a year of jobs from calls that go unanswered today.
- Outbound AI turns the member list into scheduled revenue, and an 8-point renewal lift on an assumed 6,000 members adds about $403k a year before tune-up upsell.
- At roughly $0.12 a minute for a self-built stack (or $1.67-$3 a call bought off the shelf), the cost is a rounding error against a $1,024 average repair ticket.
- The same engine runs for every portfolio company: emergency lines for CET, a password-reset desk for Frontline, reorder lines for Thomas Scientific, a press line for BPI and order help for Fair Harbor.
- Built with a clear virtual-assistant greeting, human handoff and 100% transcript QA, 24/7 voice coverage becomes a measurable, data-room-ready growth engine that raises booked revenue without adding headcount.
Pp revenue model:
Inbound calls per month: 3502
Inbound calls formula: market calls/month = (HVAC 10 + plumbing 16 + electrical 7) calls/day per 10k households (Punctual Pros demand model baselines) x 1,001,408 core housing units / 10,000 x 30.42 days = 100,516; PP share is not public, so it is backed out of revenue: PP call-driven jobs = $22M x 70% / $1,024 = 15,039/yr; inbound calls = jobs / (answer rate 0.852 x human booking rate 0.42) = 42,027/yr = 3,502/month => implied PP share of market reactive calls = 3.5%.
Market calls per month core: 100,516
Implied pp share of market calls: 0.0348
Missed share: 0.148
Missed share formula: after-hours share 0.12 x after-hours lost 0.35 + daytime share 0.88 x daytime missed/abandoned 0.12 = 0.148
Missed share range:
0.1; 0.35
Recovered share with ai: 0.8
Booking rate: 0.45
Incrementality: 0.6
Avg ticket: 1024
Recovered revenue annual ($): 1,372,000
Recovered revenue formula: 3,502 calls/mo x 12 x missed 0.148 x recovered 0.8 x booking 0.45 x incrementality 0.6 x $1,024 = 1,343 incremental jobs x $1,024 = $1,372,000 (after-hours $390,000 + daytime/storm overflow $982,000)
Outbound renewal uplift ($): 403,000
Outbound renewal formula: 6,000 members x (0.88 - 0.8) renewal lift x (fee $240 + member service revenue $600) = $403,000
Total est ($): 1,775,000
Share of pp revenue: 0.081
Sensitivity:
Missed share 0.35 invoca industry: 3,253,000
Booking 0.70 servicetitan ai: 2,140,000

Assumptions:
- Market baselines: Punctual Pros demand model HVAC 10, plumbing 16, electrical 7 reactive calls/day per 10k households (market-wide, all providers), applied to 1,001,408 core housing units (Punctual Pros nationwide plan and ZIP coverage).
- PP revenue ~$22M (repo estimate); 70% of it assumed to start with an inbound call (rest: replacements sold on site, memberships, commercial).
- Average ticket $1,024 = Housecall Pro 2025 HVAC repair revenue per job $1,205 x 0.85 to reflect lower plumbing/electrical repair tickets (assumption); LSA-sourced tickets ($1,434-$2,110) include replacements and are not used.
- Missed share 0.148: after-hours calls are ~12% of HVAC inbound (ServiceTitan 2025: 9.8% Oct to 14.1% Jun) and trades lose 30-40% of them (ServiceTitan webinar); daytime missed/abandoned 12% is an assumption for a staffed CSR team, well below Invoca's 35% industry rate for calls >15s.
- Recovered share 0.8: the AI answers every call on the first ring but some callers hang up on hearing an assistant or are not service leads (spam, vendors, wrong numbers).
- Booking rate 0.45: Invoca's 45% lead-conversion-on-call, deliberately below ServiceTitan's 70% (90% capacity-adjusted) AI booking rate because recovered calls include non-bookable calls.
- Incrementality 0.6: 40% of recovered callers are assumed to have called back or booked anyway; ServiceTitan customers describe AI-booked overflow jobs as incremental, so this is conservative.
- Renewals: 6,000 active members (assumption; replace with ServiceTitan membership count), base renewal 80% (Applause HQ), AI outbound lifts it to 88% (assumption informed by vendor-reported automated vs manual lapse rates), fee $20/month (Applause $15-30 range), $600 extra service revenue per member-year (assumption; Sera reports members spend ~2.5x non-members).
- Not counted: speed-to-lead callbacks, unsold-estimate follow-up, no-show reduction and the Spanish line (valued separately in use case items), CSR labor savings, and storm-day surge pricing.
- Calibrate every input in month 1 from ServiceTitan call-tracking (missed/abandoned by hour), booking-rate reports and membership exports; replace assumptions before quoting externally.

Read the program summary
45 AI agents cover BSP's six active companies, one set per operating system (ServiceOS, GridOS, FirmOS, LabOS, SignalOS, HarborOS), built from 8 reusable patterns. Each agent starts on an event, such as a missed call, an NWS alert, a deed record, a bid posting or an invoice, so no one has to remember to start it. Every agent also names the person who approves its consequential actions; no agent moves money, prices below a margin floor, posts publicly or disables an account on its own.On labelled analyst assumptions the program is worth about $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent value once ramped, led by Thomas Scientific ($3.8M) and Frontline ($3.6M). Punctual Pros ($0.9M) gets the most agents per dollar of revenue because missed calls, dispatch, options, memberships and permits are where home-services margin is won or lost. CET ($1.3M) uses agents to pick better bids, estimate faster and turn NuWave and EV monitoring into recurring revenue, staying inside New England.BPI ($2.3M) and Fair Harbor ($0.8M) use agents to productize monitoring, protect client confidentiality while drafting faster, and cut returns and excess inventory. Rollout runs in four waves over 18 months, starting with inbound-contact and document agents that have the clearest baselines and lowest risk, then finance, then revenue agents, then monitoring services. PRG governance sets least-privilege access, consequence-based approval tiers, full audit logs, approved model terms with no training on portfolio data, vendor AI reviews, and kill criteria tied to measured value.Values are estimates built from vendor case studies and public benchmarks with explicit haircuts; each must be re-based on the company's own 8-week baseline before it is counted in an exit narrative like Smith + Howard's.Overlay on this page: the $12.7M is a ceiling. Net of estimated run costs and risk-adjusted by value type it is $3.3M–$5.3M a year; see Program economics. Thomas Scientific's inventory agent moves to wave 2, and the wave-1 gate adds the legal-confidentiality control for Frontline.

Decision rules

Buy when the agent lives inside the system of record. If ServiceTitan, Procore or Gorgias ships it natively, speed beats differentiation; a buyer will not pay more for a home-built dispatch board.
Build when the agent's memory is BSP data. Bid go or no-go on CET's New England bid radar, weather surge on Punctual Pros' storm history, grant signals from NIH RePORTER, docket tracking: that scoring is the IP that makes an OS an OS at exit.
Hybrid by default for documents. Buy extraction or transport (Conexiom, Vic.ai, Intapp), build the exception queue, disclosure and audit layer once and reuse it across companies.
Every purchase passes the vendor AI review (control 5). A 30-day pilot against the company's own baseline, SOC 2 Type II, no training on portfolio data, and an exit and export clause.
Never single-source the model. Route small models to extraction and frontier models to drafting; keep a second provider qualified for failover (control 4).

Why this page
Design and program rationale
An operating partner should be able to approve a wave in one meeting, and a buyer should see the controls behind the value.

One system, not a feature dumpGive every agent the same anatomy: trigger, agent, approver. Forty-five then scan as one system.KPI: time to approve a wave; agents stopped vs shipped per quarter.
Controls up frontShow the controls, owners and evidence before anyone asks for them.KPI: diligence questions answered from the page; tier-3 incidents (target 0).
Lead with the numberOne headline figure, with its cost and risk-adjusted net beside it. Every figure stays an estimate until measured.KPI: share of the $12.7M ceiling re-based on measured baselines; capacity value counted only with a hiring plan.
Institutional tone, sources on every claimSober type and a source on every claim. It should read as a memo, not a pitch.KPI: agents backed by a measured result at a comparable company: 16 of 45 today (10 more cite a benchmark, 19 only context); target 45 of 45 via pilots.

Approve wave 1, measure for 90 days.
Six agents, controls 1–5 live everywhere, and a day-90 review against 8-week baselines. Track it in the portal's tech-enablement module.

GridOS · for CET
Every bid, crew and asset on one operating layer.
GridOS turns three project shops into one service company. It finds the work, runs the field and monitors what CET installs, so more revenue repeats.
Terms: SCADA: the control software that runs plants and pump stations. WPCA: a town water pollution control authority. SRF: state revolving fund for water projects. O&M: operations and maintenance. NEVI: the federal EV-charger program.

HighField adoptionForemen reject another app; data stays in notebooks and the dashboards go stale.Hedge: mobile-first, one foreman champion per office, daily-log completion tied to job bonuses.

02 · A day of calls
The leaks cluster when nobody is at the desk
About 115 calls a day reach Punctual Pros' brand linesest.. When they arrive, how many go unanswered, and the same day with an AI agent on ring one.

What happens today

After 5 p.m. and on weekends, calls go to voicemail or an answering service that takes a message. Trades lose 30–40% of these calls.
At lunch and on storm days, customer service reps are already on the phone, so about 12% of daytime calls ring out or are abandoned (assumption).
The caller hangs up and calls the next company listed on Google.

With 24/7 voice coverage

Every call is answered on the first ring with the brand greeting, and the agent says it is the virtual assistant.
The agent runs the safety screen, finds the customer in ServiceTitan, offers open capacity and books the job.
Reps stay on the calls they are already handling. Hazards, VIPs and complaints are warm-transferred with a summary.

Fast handoff to a person, every call scored
Rules for every call at every company: when a person takes over, how calls are scored and how changes are tested.

Escalation and human-handoff SLAs
Portfolio policy. Safety hazard → warm transfer to on-call within 60 s (else 911/utility instruction + page); explicit second request for a human → transfer within 60 s business hours, callback within 10 min after hours; complaint/billing dispute → human same day; weekly review of every escalation; target escalation rate 10-20% in month 1, falling with tuning.
Vendors build live escalation into AI CSRs (ServiceTitan: live escalation to human agents; Cresta at Brinks Home cut transfers from 30% to 8% while raising FCR to 92%). The aim is fewer transfers that land faster, not zero transfers.

Score 100% of calls automatically against a rubric (greeting, safety screen, booking asked, fee wording, tone); humans review a 5% weighted sample plus all escalations and complaints; re-run a fixed test-call suite before any prompt/model/voice change; treat a wrong safety instruction or unauthorized price as a P1 incident with a 48-hour root-cause note.
NIST AI 600-1 (Generative AI Profile, July 2024) recommends documented pre-launch testing, ongoing monitoring and incident response for generative AI; the portfolio AI-agent plan (control 3) sets 3-7 year log retention by company.

Design rationale
Why this page looks and works the way it does
Make the case in 90 seconds, then survive diligence on every input.

A clock instead of a slideA running counter makes the cost of waiting concrete. It is labelled as a model, with the formula one click away.
Hear it before you believe itPeople judge voice AI by listening to it. The demo shows the agent booking jobs, not taking messages.

The short version
Thesis first, essential services, founders stay
Twelve observations, each traceable to a press release or a filing. Weights and strengths are analyst inference from the public record, not BSP’s internal criteria.

BSP buys theme-first: each deal release frames the company as the output of a sector thesis studied in advance, from RJ David's 'over a year' in electrical services before CET to Adam Glucksman's watch on accounting before Smith + Howard.Since 2024 the filter has narrowed to essential services. Punctual Pros, Frontline and CET are all non-discretionary, and Fair Harbor remains the only discretionary consumer bet and the only portfolio company besides Frontline with no add-ons.Anchor acquisitions come from two kinds of seller: sponsor secondaries for the larger checks (Thomas from Carlyle, BPI from Svoboda, Frontline from BV) and founder or partner owners taking first institutional capital for the smaller ones (Fair Harbor, Smith + Howard, Punctual Pros, CET).In secondaries the outgoing sponsor often rolls a minority (Svoboda at BPI, BV at Frontline), and the inherited CEO is replaced at about 13-15 months (Simmons to Haas at Thomas, Naidoo to Britt at Frontline) while founder CEOs such as Sean Taylor, Matt Buckwalter and John Duquette Jr. stay.Anchor acquisitions are bought in banked processes (6 of 7 had a named sell-side adviser, and Punctual Pros went to 'eight finalists'). Berenson advised BSP on Thomas, BPI, Frontline and CET, Harris Williams on Punctual Pros and Frontline, and Morrison Cohen or Greenberg Traurig was counsel on every deal.The first add-on typically closes 6-9 months after the anchor acquisition (NCI at 6.1 months, BOLDT 7.6, Horvath 8.0, NuWave 8.0, Market Street 9.0), and the median is 8.0 months.Add-ons are small founder-, family- or partner-owned firms (Day Associates with 10 people, Smith Kesler with 30+, Horton with 120+). None of the 21 identified came from a PE seller, and many were sourced through relationships, such as Matt Buckwalter's decade-long tie to Horvath.Add-ons alternate between filling in geography (Market Street, Smith Kesler, Horton Lee & Burnett, Horvath, Horton) and adding new capabilities that create cross-sell (VIP, Fahrenheit, Geels Norton, Message House, Agado, NuWave).Each company is financed with a private-credit unitranche from a different direct lender (Apollo/MidCap at Thomas, PineBridge at BPI, PGIM at Punctual Pros, NXT and Audax at Frontline), with delayed-draw or amendment capacity sized for the add-on program.Larger companies get a deal-named co-invest SPV (BSP-TS, BSP-BPI Holdings, BSP-FL, BSP-CET). Against a $335M Fund I, a company needing more than about $40M of equity depends on co-investors such as Carlyle AlpInvest.Smith + Howard is the template so far: about 100 professionals grew to about 800 through 9 add-ons and a tech, AI and offshore build-out, and the firm was sold to TPG Growth after 3.7 years with William Blair and Baird running the process.Thomas Scientific shows the value of leaving room in the debt for add-ons and a refinancing. For the next deals the implied rubric favors $3-20M EBITDA essential-services leaders in fragmented regional markets with a founder CEO who will stay and run M&A, a warm first add-on, and a credible tech-enablement story.

Six practices work as one team: public affairs, corporate reputation, campaigns, research, digital and paid media, and AI communications.Which offices do you have?Washington, DC (headquarters), New York, Chicago, San Francisco, Los Angeles and Boston in the US; London, Brussels, Berlin, Oslo and Zurich/Geneva in Europe; and Asia-Pacific coverage through the Mandala Partners alliance in Australia.What is SignalOS?SignalOS is the proposed intelligence layer under every BPI retainer: always-on narrative monitoring, synthetic-audience message testing validated with live panels, a compliance-gated content studio and outcome dashboards. It turns monitoring and measurement into a subscription rather than a line item.How do retainers and pricing work?Most work runs on monthly retainers; campaigns and research are scoped as projects. The concept adds three tiers (Monitor, Advise, Command) with illustrative prices.How fast can you respond in a crisis?Under the proposed SignalOS retainers, alerts arrive with a draft holding statement. The response target is 2 hours on Monitor and 30 minutes on Advise and Command.Can you test our message before we launch it?Yes. Message House, the elite-audience research group BPI acquired in Nov 2024, tests messages with policymakers, investors and other hard-to-reach audiences across EMEA. SignalOS adds synthetic pre-tests that narrow options in hours before live fieldwork confirms the finalists.Do you work in Brussels and Berlin?Yes. BOLDT (December 2023) and 365 Sherpas (May 2026) made Germany BPI’s third-largest market. One retainer can cover Washington, Brussels and Berlin.What is AI communications?AI policy positioning, deepfake and misinformation response, and AI-assisted content with review checkpoints. In BPI’s 2026 survey, 81% of adults said AI spreads false rumours too easily.Do you work with sports organizations?Yes. BPI formalized a sports offering in Oct 2024 and scaled it with the May 2025 acquisition of Agado Communications, whose founder Mark Jones leads BPI’s sports strategy and growth.Do you handle litigation and regulatory risk?Yes. In Mar 2026 BPI launched a litigation communications, oversight and regulatory-risk offering led by partner Elizabeth E. Alexander, covering congressional oversight, investigations and enforcement actions.Who leads BPI?Andrew Bleeker is CEO and Ben LaBolt has been President since Apr 2025. BSP made a majority investment in Apr 2023; Svoboda Capital Partners remains an investor.Are you hiring?The concept careers section lists illustrative openings across public affairs, research, SignalOS data engineering and corporate affairs in Washington, New York, London, Berlin and Chicago.How do I start a conversation?Use the contact form: pick a topic (public affairs, reputation, campaign, research, crisis or a SignalOS briefing) and the right partner follows up. Design rationale

Lead with the numberPut the four numbers the deal team gets asked about on the first screen.
Entry to exit on a dated timelineFollow the dated path of a plan that already produced an exit.
Show coverage, not logosMaps show density and reach; a list of logos does not.
Answers on demandLet a partner ask the plan a question and get an answer from the same data.

Design principles
Ten rules every concept follows.
Drawn from sponsor-owned peers and category leaders, each tied to the KPI it should move.

01One primary action above the fold, attached to the input.A headline, one field and one button: a ZIP code, an email or a chat prompt. Everything else is a ghost button or a link.KPI: Hero click-through, questions asked per visit and booked jobs per session.
02Show live, real numbers early; scale beats adjectives.A stat band computed from real data (ZIP codes, opportunities, staff, locations) with units and a source line. Illustrative figures are always labelled.KPI: Scroll depth past the stat band, time on page and credibility in user tests.
03Show the product, not stock imagery.Real interface screenshots in device frames, or a working demo such as a dispatch board, a bid board or trust controls. Each OS page leads with its interactive demo.KPI: Demo interactions, tour starts and demo-to-contact conversion.
04Put proof at the point of decision.Rating, review count and licences sit beside the call to action, never only on an About page.KPI: Call and booking conversion and lead-to-opportunity rate.
05Make coverage the first question for physical-service businesses.A location chip, ZIP check or service-area finder in or next to the hero, wired to real coverage data: the Punctual Pros ZIP-code model and CET's six New England states.KPI: Out-of-area call rate down and qualified-lead share up.
06Productize the service into a named offer.Give the recurring program a name and a page of its own. Each portfolio OS page (ServiceOS, GridOS, FirmOS, LabOS, SignalOS, HarborOS) follows this pattern.KPI: Recurring share of revenue, membership and contract attach, and exit multiple.
07Make the company and acquisition story visible.An Acquisitions or Partner with us link in the main navigation, founder stories and brand counts turn the website into a proprietary sourcing channel for add-ons.KPI: Inbound seller conversations per quarter and share of add-ons sourced directly.
08Give buyers self-serve tools for the jobs they repeat.Calculators, price estimators, quick order, order history, documents and client portals, placed in the header or a utility bar rather than the footer.KPI: Tool completions to leads, reorder rate and support tickets per account.
09Neutral base, one accent; typography carries the brand.An off-white or near-black canvas, one accent for actions and a mono face for numbers. Colour carries meaning, never decoration.KPI: Perceived quality in user tests and call-to-action salience.
10Offer an assistant grounded in your own data, placed where questions come up.An Ask panel over the company's own data and FAQ, with example questions and labelled sources.KPI: Questions answered without a person, assisted conversion and returns rate.

Source: design references, 26 reference homepages reviewed and captured on October 6, 2026.

The rationale
Why a better website plus an OS raises portfolio value.
Buyers pay for earnings that look predictable, recurring and scalable. A better site and an OS move those through six levers.

Lever 01ConversionThe website is the cheapest growth lever a services business owns. Coverage checks and instant booking turn the same traffic into more jobs.38% vs 59%HVAC inbound call booking rate, average shop versus shops with 25+ technicians (ServiceTitan benchmark)
Lever 02Recurring revenueNamed offers such as memberships, maintenance contracts and monitoring subscriptions move revenue from project to repeatable, which is what buyers pay up for.5–6x vs 10x+EBITDA multiples for project-heavy versus repeatable-service HVAC businesses (PKF)
Lever 03Cost to serveSelf-serve tools (quick order, punchout, portals, calculators) take routine work off reps and service desks and win long-tail share.+15.6% vs ~2%Grainger digital Endless Assortment growth versus rep-led High-Touch, 2025
Lever 04RetentionFit tools, replenishment and client portals keep customers longer and cut costly returns.+5 pts → +25–95%profit lift from five points of retention (Bain via HBR); online apparel returns run 19.3% (NRF)
Lever 05MultipleVisible, data-backed KPIs let the next buyer underwrite quality, which is where the spread between typical and premium deals sits.6.8x vs 9.8xtypical versus premium middle-market EBITDA multiples, a spread of about three turns (Capstone, IMAP)
Lever 06Buy-and-buildOne OS is the integration layer every add-on plugs into, and the site is a proprietary sourcing channel for the next one.~17–18.5xreported multiples for scaled, systems-led home-services companies (Sila, Champions)

text:
Growth plan · October 2026
Fair Harbor: from a summer swim brand to a year-round lifestyle brand.
New categories, more wholesale doors, retention, then international, financed capital-light.
Terms: ABL: asset-based loan, secured on inventory. GMV: gross merchandise value. WISMO: “where is my order?” contacts. IRR: internal rate of return.

See the 36-month plan
HarborOS
Open in portal

Every financial figure on this page is an analyst assumptionest. built from public filings. Fair Harbor has never disclosed revenue, EBITDA or debt.

Today → month 36est.
Net revenue$27M →$40M+48% · 14.0%/yr · today’s range $20–35MEBITDA$1.6M →$5.2M6.0% → 13.0% marginDoors + owned stores254 →522+268 doors · 2.1xRevenue per employee$450K →$571Kheadcount 60 → 70
Read this as recovery first. Our outside-in estimate puts revenue at or below its 2021 entry scale (est. $30–40M). The plan gets back to the top of that range by month 36 (Oct 2029). Bar = today as a share of month 36. Analyst assumptions, not company guidance.

The memo in 60 seconds
Fix the base, then buy growth with doors, not debt.
Each line is grounded in filings, comparables and vendor evidence. Estimates say so.

Memo · 13 pointsThis starts from a hypothesis for management to confirm. If our outside-in estimate is right (~$27M of revenue, range $20–35M, built from web traffic rather than company data), Fair Harbor is about 4.5 years in and at or below its 2021 entry scale (est. $30–40M), with low single-digit EBITDA and no add-ons.The shift to a year-round lifestyle brand has already happened on the shelf: 64.0% of the 372 live products are non-swim, and golf, kids, collegiate and B2B custom launched in 2025–2026.Margin is the problem: 38.5% of live variants are marked down, women's was cleared at ~70% off, and swim is the most-returned category at Shopify brands (21.6%).So the first six months are about fixing the base (markdown discipline, fit and returns, and buying to forecast) before we pay for growth.Chubbies is the proof case for the next step: at $122.9M it takes 51.9% of sales from wholesale and retail, that channel grew 16.3% last year, and its DTC fell 20.8% in Q2 2026.Our plan is to take Fair Harbor from ~250 specialty doors to ~520 over 36 months through golf pro shops, campus bookstores and coastal specialty, using commissioned reps rather than new owned stores.Retention is the cheapest growth: repeat-purchase benchmarks are 20–30%, and Klaviyo flows earn about 41% of email revenue from 5% of sends.HarborOS, at an est. $0.3–0.7M, puts nine agents on that work (fit, CX, returns-to-exchange, demand planning, markdowns, lifecycle, paid media, cross-border and wholesale reorders); vendor claims include 60% ticket automation and 17% fewer fit returns.International starts in month 30 as merchant-of-record DTC into Canada, the UK and Australia, following Vuori's e-commerce-first launch, because the store ships only to the US today.We should stay capital-light: operating cash and an ABL of roughly $3.4–4.6M (est.) cover the plan, with a small sponsor follow-on as the backstop. Solo Brands' delisting shows what term debt does to a swim brand.The roadmap assumes revenue grows from ~$27M to ~$40M and EBITDA from ~$1.6M to ~$5.2M by month 36. That is still below Chubbies' 18% margin, and every figure is an analyst assumption, not company data. On revenue, that only takes the business back to the top of the estimated entry range.Measured from entry, the default exit case is weak: about 1.38x the est. entry EV midpoint over ~7.5 years, roughly 4.4% a year of EV growth. Measured from today's value at the same multiple, it earns about 21% a year. So the real decision is exit timing, which the Financing section sets out.The Smith + Howard lesson applies: buyers paid for a scaled, legible portfolio company, so the exit story is wholesale breadth, repeat-customer economics and margin, and the logical buyers are strategics and brand owners.

The template
Smith + Howard showed what a buyer pays for. Here is the consumer version.
Smith + Howard grew from one office to 11 with 9 add-ons and ~4x revenue. Fair Harbor’s “offices” are doors and channels.

Template · exited Aug 2026Smith + Howard~100 → ~800 professionals, 1 → 11 offices, 9 add-ons, sold to TPG GrowthRevenue multiple4.0xFootprint multiple11.0xPeople multiple8.0xAcquisitions9Years held3.5Plan · entry Mar 2022 → exit Oct 2029Fair Harbor planest.$27M today → $40M revenue at month 36, 254 → 522 doors, headcount held near 70, no acquisitions assumedRevenue multiple1.1xFootprint multiple2.1xPeople multiple1.2xAcquisitions0Years held7.5
Source: BSP exit release and the Fair Harbor growth plan, Oct 2026. Fair Harbor's revenue multiple is measured from the 2021 entry-year estimate (midpoint $35M), not from today. Footprint and people are measured from today, because entry-year counts aren't public. A month-36 exit (Oct 2029) is ~7.5 years after BSP's March 2022 entry, about twice the Smith + Howard hold.
Step 1 · Smith + HowardEntry: founder-led regional leader, first institutional capitalBSP made a strategic anchor investment in Smith + Howard (Atlanta, ~100 professionals, one office) in Nov 2022.Fair Harbor translation. Fair Harbor is the same set-up in consumer: a founder-led brand taking its first institutional capital ($30.7M Form D, Mar 2022). The S+H lesson is that the entry thesis named the adjacent services up front; Fair Harbor's equivalent is a named category-and-channel map (year-round apparel, golf, collegiate, B2B, international).Step 2 · Smith + HowardFirst adjacent-market step: merge with a like-minded firm next doorMerged with Market Street Partners (Chattanooga) in Aug 2023, its first move beyond Atlanta.Fair Harbor translation. For Fair Harbor the 'next city' is the next door type: green-grass golf pro shops via FootJoy (18 collab SKUs) and sporting-goods doors like Scheels, before any new owned store.Step 3 · Smith + HowardCapability add-ons that widen the menu sold to existing clientsAdded benefit-plan audit (JMM CPAs, Chicago, Jan 2024) and executive search (VIP Search/VIP Solutions, Dallas, Apr 2024).Fair Harbor translation. Category extension is Fair Harbor's version: 372 live products, 64.0% of them non-swim, plus kids (51) and B2B custom (88 SKUs). Every new category should be sold first to the existing customer file and the existing door list.Step 4 · Smith + HowardDensity in a chosen region, deal after dealFahrenheit Advisors (Richmond, Dec 2024), Smith Kesler (Carolinas, Jan 2025), Horton Lee & Burnett (Birmingham, Sep 2025), Bauknight Pietras & Stormer (SC, Jan 2026).Fair Harbor translation. Fair Harbor should build door density in its proven coastal and golf geographies (Northeast, Florida, the Carolinas) before spreading thin, so reps, trunk shows and co-op marketing are shared across doors.Step 5 · Smith + HowardTechnology, AI and offshore delivery as the margin enginePer the exit release, BSP invested in leadership, technology, AI-enabled capabilities and an offshore delivery centre in India; Geels Norton (cyber, Feb 2026) added a tech-heavy service line.Fair Harbor translation. HarborOS is the consumer equivalent: fit/size, CX, returns-to-exchange and demand-planning agents on Shopify/Klaviyo, sized at $0.3–0.7M for 2–5 points of EBITDA margin (ServiceOS evidence, est.).Step 6 · Smith + HowardThe exit: a scaled, buyer-legible portfolio company sold to a growth investorSold to TPG (TPG Growth), closed Aug 6 2026 after ~3.5 years: ~100 to ~800 professionals, 1 to 11 Southeast locations plus India, 9 add-ons, nearly 4x revenue.Fair Harbor translation. Fair Harbor is ~4.5 years into its hold with no add-ons. The S+H template says the exit story must be a scaled company with visible recurring earnings; for a brand that means wholesale breadth, repeat-customer economics and margin, not just top-line.
Vertical analog 1Chubbies (Solo Brands)Net sales FY2025: $122.9MWholesale retail share: 51.9%Segment EBITDA margin: 18.2%Acquisition price: $129.5MThis is the clearest proof that wholesale breadth, not DTC alone, carries a men's swim brand past $100M; and that a leveraged owner (Solo was delisted in July 2026 with ~$249M debt) can damage a good brand. It is also a possible add-on or door-share opportunity if Chubbies is sold.Source: sec.govConfidence: highVertical analog 2VuoriInternational markets 2022: 7Valuation 2021: $4BUS store plan: 100International should start as localized DTC in English-speaking coastal markets with a merchant-of-record partner and a few premium wholesale partners, as Vuori did, not with owned stores.Source: mr-mag.comConfidence: mediumVertical analog 3Faherty BrandBrand value or revenue: $250MStores: 80Founded: 2013The closest positioning analog to Fair Harbor (coastal, year-round lifestyle). It shows the ceiling of the category, but its store-heavy route is capital-intensive; Fair Harbor should borrow the specialty-door relationships and year-round assortment, not the 80-store fleet.Source: guyraz.substack.comConfidence: medium

Risks
What could break the plan, and what we do about it.
Severity is an analyst call. Each risk links to its public evidence.

Risk 1 · High severityThe baseline itself is an estimateFair Harbor has never disclosed revenue, EBITDA or debt; the $27M / 6% baseline is the midpoint of a $20–35M, 0–12% low-confidence range, and it sits at or below the est. 2021 entry scale.Mitigation. Lock targets only after a monthly KPI pack (Ask 1). Re-base the roadmap, not the thesis.Risk 2 · High severityMarkdown dependence erodes the brand38.5% of live variants were marked down in Sept 2026 and the women's line was cleared at ~70% off (live Shopify catalog, 24 Sep 2026; women's update page, Dec 2025).Mitigation. Markdown guardrail (Ask 4), planning hire, markdown agent on SKU-level end-of-season pricing.Risk 3 · High severityWeather and a single peak seasonSwim is the most-returned category at Shopify brands (21.6%, an industry benchmark) and sales peak May–July; a cold, wet summer hits revenue and inventory together.Mitigation. Grow non-swim from 64% toward 70% of the assortment, buy to forecast, size the ABL to the seasonal build.Risk 4 · Medium severityDTC demand is softening across the categoryFair Harbor web visits fell 19.6% month on month (Similarweb, Aug 2026); Chubbies DTC fell 20.8% in Q2 2026.Mitigation. Shift mix toward wholesale (~50% by M36) and retention flows before raising paid spend.Risk 5 · Medium severityWholesale credit exposureFair Harbor appears in the J.Crew (2020) and Express (2024) bankruptcy dockets (CourtListener); more doors means more receivables.Mitigation. Credit limits by account tier, credit insurance on department-store AR, diversify into golf and campus doors.Risk 6 · Medium severityWebsite accessibility litigationTwo ADA website suits in S.D.N.Y. (2024, settled; Jul 2026, open) (CourtListener).Mitigation. Fold a WCAG 2.2 AA remediation into the HarborOS PDP and checkout work in phase 1.Risk 7 · Medium severityUnknown current lender and covenantsThe eCapital ABL lien was released on Dec 11, 2025, the same day the core marks moved to a Topco; the new facility is not public (USPTO lien records).Mitigation. Confirm facility, covenants and borrowing base (Ask 5); no term debt until EBITDA clears ~$4–5M.Risk 8 · Low severityAI vendor claims are upper boundsEvery agent metric is vendor- or research-reported and self-selected.Mitigation. Pilot each agent with a holdout group; pay-per-resolution pricing where offered.

Enterprise value = EBITDA × multiple. Today: $8M × 6.8x = $54.4M. Month 36: $30M × (6.8x + 1.0 turn) = $234M, or 4.3x today's EV, gross of add-on capital. Not all of that is created: at ~8% organic growth CET reaches ~$101M of revenue on its own, so ~$139M of the $240M is bought. That brings ~$13.9M of EBITDA at an est. 5.5x, or ~$76.6M of capital paid for add-ons. Net of that capital, month-36 value is $157M, $103M above today. Capstone/IMAP put typical middle-market deals at 6.8x and premium deals at 9.8x. PKF puts project-heavy contractors at 5–6x and repeatable service at 10x+. The GridOS evidence base credits CET with 0.5–1.5 turns. All figures are estimatesest.. Source: CET growth plan roadmap, GridOS evidence base, Capstone and IMAP 2026 survey, PKF summer 2026 update.

08 · Eyes open
What could go wrong, and what we need from the PRG.

Risks and mitigationsHighEvery baseline is an estimateRevenue, EBITDA, headcount and margin come from PPP payroll, revenue per employee and peer margins (low confidence). CET does not disclose them.Mitigation: Run a 30-day data request and re-base the roadmap and the lever baselines on actuals before the next board meeting.HighLicensed electricians are scarceBLS expects ~81,000 electrician openings a year, and ABC says 499K net new construction workers are needed in 2026. Growth stalls if crews can’t be staffed.Mitigation: Two apprenticeship lanes, tax-credit capture, a journeyman fast track and broad-based equity for foremen (section 05).HighHorton integration and key peopleHorton is third-generation and founder-led, and it holds the CT wastewater relationships. McKinsey finds ~70% of mergers miss their revenue-synergy targets.Mitigation: Keep the brand and the 24/7 crews. Sign retention agreements with named managers. Integrate the back office first and the field last.MediumSponsors competing for the same targets15 New England electrical/energy firms are already sponsor-owned. 16 PE firms overlap with CET, 5 rated high threat. Crete United’s RELCO is ~10 miles from Taunton.Mitigation: Lead with founder rollover and a partner model where brands stay, plus proprietary owner-succession outreach, not banker auctions.MediumThe second-ring target pool is thin15 RI/NH/ME/VT targets are screened and none scores ≥ 70. Maine, NH and VT plants are not yet in the wastewater screen.Mitigation: Run an outreach-led sourcing pass through NECA and IEC chapters, and extend the wastewater screen to ME, NH and VT SRF lists.MediumBonding capacity and public-bid exposureSurety capacity, debt terms and DCAMM certification are not public. SRF project values are applicant estimates, not awards.Mitigation: Arrange surety introductions early. Bid selectively through GridOS go/no-go scoring, and keep public hard-bid work below a set share of backlog.MediumUnion and merit-shop mixCET shows as non-union on OSHA records, and several targets (e.g., McDonald’s ANJ division, Murphy, Averill) are union. That limits which crews can take which public or utility jobs.Mitigation: Run union add-ons as divisions alongside the IEC merit-shop lane. Don’t convert either.LowData-center hypeISO-NE says New England data-center load lags other regions, so data-center electrical is upside, not the core of the plan.Mitigation: Price it as an option. GridOS value is booked only inside the 0.5–1.5-turn evidence range.Beyond this plan, not in the numbers. Any move into NY, NJ or eastern PA would be a separate board decision at month 24, and only if month-24 revenue and margin are at or above plan ($170M, 11.5%). The $240M month-36 figure does not depend on it. New York City is out either way.
Asks of the PRGA 30-day data request: actual revenue, EBITDA, backlog, recurring share, utilization and bid-hit ratio by state, to replace every est. on this page. Nov 2026Approve the GridOS budget ($800K–$1.8M): start with the three fastest agents: 24/7 dispatcher (3 wks), bid-radar triage (4 wks) and contract review (4 wks). Q4 2026Sourcing support: owner-succession outreach in RI, NH, ME and VT, introductions to NECA and IEC chapters, and LOIs for two MA tuck-ins from the top of the screen. Phase 1Capital: confirm delayed-draw capacity (lower middle market averages ~4.0x total leverage) and line up co-invest for the Phase 2 wave, following the BSP-CET Co-Invest precedent. by month 9Surety and bonding introductions: to support public wastewater and SRF-funded bids at a larger size. Q1 2027People design: an equity pool for licensed electricians and foremen, plus a plan to claim MA RATC (up to $100K per employer) and the CT apprenticeship credit. Q1 2027

Method
Sources, caveats and why the page looks this way.

Method, sources and caveats every source and link behind the numbersMethod. Template events come from BSP, Smith + Howard and trade-press releases (Accounting Today, CPA Practice Advisor), checked Oct 6, 2026. Vertical analogs (Pfingsten NEC Group, Ridgemont Crete United, Kohlberg Loenbro, IES Holdings) come from PE Hub, PrivSource and SEC 8-K filings. Phase figures are computed from the portal's research: the bid radar (86 items), the wastewater screen (183 plants), the add-on screen (48 targets), the county fit model (67 counties), our filings review and the GridOS evidence base. Every revenue, EBITDA, headcount and margin target is an analyst assumption anchored to filings-based estimates.
Wastewater dollars. The page uses one measure: funded or requested plant and pump-station projects on the CT, MA and RI state lists, at the applicant's total project cost (the first-listed project per plant). The underlying screen also carries a broader "pipeline" total that adds every facility-related line, including collection-system and tributary-town work. It is larger and is not used here. Neither figure is an award or CET's electrical scope.
CaveatsAll CET revenue, EBITDA, headcount and margin baselines are low-confidence analyst estimates from CET filings (PPP payroll, revenue per employee, comp margins). None is disclosed by CET or BSP. KPI roadmap and KPI targets are labelled assumptions, not guidance.Management guidance is a New England focus with no NYC expansion. This plan and every number on this page are New England only. A move into NY, NJ or eastern PA would be a separate board decision and is not modelled.Smith + Howard add-on count: BSP's release says nine; named transactions reconcile to nine only if VIP Search and VIP Solutions count separately (see Punctual Pros nationwide plan caveats). Their claims were taken from search-engine extracts of those pages on Oct 6, 2026 and should be spot-checked before external use.AI-agent metrics are vendor case studies or vendor claims for selected customers (Togal, Document Crunch, Bridgit, Newmetrix, Samotics, ServiceTitan), not controlled studies. Several come from general contractors or residential trades and are extrapolated to an electrical subcontractor. The Samotics figure is in GBP for a UK utility.The FMI Capital Advisors 9-11x vs 6.5-8.5x recurring-service multiple claim is second-hand (quoted in a ServiceTitan blog, mechanical-contractor benchmarks) and was not read in the FMI original.CET opportunity radar estimated value is populated for only 43 of 86 items and reflects total project or program cost, not CET's electrical scope. WWTP project values are applicant estimates on draft/final SRF lists, not awards. Maine, NH and VT plants are not in CET wastewater-plant targets.CET add-on targets revenue is ZoomInfo modeled; several figures conflict with headcount (e.g., JM Electrical $91M with 74 staff). Ownership is unknown for 26 of 48 targets.CET appears as non-union on OSHA records (entity identity not independently confirmed). Union/merit-shop status of add-ons will constrain which apprenticeship lane and which public/utility work each crew can take.Bonding/surety capacity, debt terms and DCAMM certification are not public (CET filings data gaps). Growth marketing · October 2026
ZIP-targeted TV, not the whole market.
Sell the on-time promise the three brands already own. Local Services Ads are the base; ZIP-targeted TV, new-mover mail and weather triggers build on it.
Terms: LSA: Google Local Services Ads. CTV: connected TV. VO: voiceover. ROAS: return on ad spend. DMA: a TV market area. NWS: National Weather Service.

Run the numbers
Watch the sample spots

Conservative case for Phase 1 (Central PA, Nov 2026 – Apr 2027): attributed jobs cut for incrementality (LSA, search and Meta 50%; CTV and mail 75%), contribution after technician labour, materials and ~7.5% franchise fees. At this level the plan adds ~12% to Punctual Pros’ ~$22M revenue and needs ~3 more technicians. Every figure is est. until the test reads it.

Sample :15 · “Storm Ready” · One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning®

No active NWS alerts in Punctual Pros’ 11 counties (checked 7:01 AM). CTV runs at base weight.

1Local Services Ads base$39–57 per lead at a ~44% book rate (SearchLight, Feb 2026). Ranked by reviews and answer speed.
2ZIP-targeted CTV~$15–40 CPM, starting in 61 Tier-I ZIPs (336k homes). Bought by ZIP, so spend stays near Punctual Pros’ footprint.
3New-mover mail~2,300 PA and ~1,150 NJ arm’s-length home buyers a month (floor), from the county deed feeds already in the portal.
4Weather triggersA National Weather Service warning for a Punctual Pros county adds 50% to CTV for 72 hours and puts the storm cut live. It re-times spend: ~$5k a year at Phase 1 weights.
Read the full ten-point thesisPunctual Pros' three franchise brands all promise punctuality, so the ads should sell that promise (One Hour's 'Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!', Ben Franklin's $5-a-minute guarantee, Mister Sparky's 'America's On-Time Electrician') rather than invent new claims.Google Local Services Ads are the cheapest high-intent leads in the category ($39-57 per lead at a ~44% book rate, SearchLight Feb 2026), so LSA is the always-on base and is managed through reviews and fast answer rates rather than bids.Self-serve CTV has dropped to $50-$500 minimums and roughly $15-40 CPMs with zip targeting (Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads, YouTube on TV screens), which lets a ~$22M franchisee buy TV in its ~240 zips without paying for the whole Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA.CTV's job is to make the brand familiar before the furnace fails and to lift branded search and LSA conversion, so it is judged on cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift, not completion rate (which is ~94-99% by construction).New-mover direct mail is the highest-intent prospect list a home-services company can get: county deed records show ~2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core and ~1,150 on the Jersey Shore, each a household that must pick an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider within months.One in three of those PA buyers bought a pre-1980 home, which drives the Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky older-home inspection offers and the CTV zip weighting toward older housing stock (Punctual Pros ZIP coverage older-housing share).The weather index ties it together: NWS alerts for Punctual Pros' zones (the demand model's weather-response plans) trigger budget multipliers and creative swaps 12-36 hours before demand spikes, so spend lands when calls are about to rise rather than after phones are already full.The same deed feed becomes the CTV and Meta audience (address-matched households) and the mail list, so one new mover sees a coordinated welcome across mailbox, TV and phone, measured against a random holdout.Test first with an 8-week, $50k/month Central PA pilot: LSA profile and review clean-up, a zip-level CTV geo holdout in the 61 Tier-I zips, and a mail-versus-holdout new-mover drip, all on unique call-tracking numbers in ServiceTitan.If measured cost per booked job beats the modelled ~$185-200 blended, scale to the Jersey Shore (zip-only CTV) and then a regional Mid-Atlantic program, which also leaves a documented, attributed customer-acquisition engine for the exit data room.

00 · Baseline

Stop CTV if…At week 12 the upper end of the 90% confidence interval on holdout lift is below break-even. An 8-week read with 9 dark zips cannot detect anything under ~44%, so “no lift at week 8” is not evidence either way. Completion rate is never the reason to keep spending.

Precedents · October 2026
How sponsors built and sold companies like Punctual Pros.
Thirty-four companies, 1996 to 2026: what each owner did, in what order, and what the next buyer paid. Punctual Pros is about 30 months in.
Terms: MOIC: multiple on invested capital. LTM: last twelve months. PIK: interest paid in more debt instead of cash.

Source: Value-creation case set: 237 dated events from sponsor and company releases, SEC and Companies House filings and trade press, retrieved Oct 2026. Exit multiples and growth are estimates.
The six moves, in order1Day 0–6Put an operator team in chargeApex Service Partners: $100M+ equity commitmentPunctual Pros · Done2Months 2–21 (median ~7)Buy the first add-on early, close to homeSmith + Howard: add-on #1; first new state (TN)Punctual Pros · Done3Months 12–48Keep tuck-ins coming every few monthsSmith + Howard: add-on #2; 30 EBP-dedicated staff; combined practice serves 500+ plansPunctual Pros · Behind4Months 0–24Run every brand on one systemChampions Group: 60,000+ members; single IT systemPunctual Pros · Partly done5Years 1–5Build recurring members buyers pay forChampions Group: Active members: 60,000 → 150,000 membersPunctual Pros · Unknown6Years 2–5Own the technician pipelineChampions Group: Field technicians: 850 → 1,800 techniciansPunctual Pros · In progress

Read the full story · the pattern across all 34 cases in one page
Across 34 cases from 1996 to 2026, the highest-value exits did the same six things in roughly the same order; Punctual Pros is about 30 months into its own version. First, the sponsor put an operator team in charge at entry: Alpine named Apex's CEO and CFO on launch day in July 2019 with $100M+ of committed equity, American Capital gave Service Experts' returning CEO about 10% ownership, and Huron recruited Sciens' CEO before it bought its first company. Second, the first add-on came early and close to home, a median of about 7 months after entry across 11 dated cases, as Smith + Howard did with Market Street Partners in month 9 and Punctual Pros did with Horvath in month 8.Third, the tuck-ins kept coming at roughly one every three to five months: Trivest did 16 at TurnPoint while revenue grew nearly 10x, Huron did 13 at Sciens while revenue and EBITDA rose more than 35x, and BSP did nine at Smith + Howard while headcount went from about 100 to about 800. Fourth, every brand ran on one system: CenterOak ran a single IT system and consolidated purchasing at Service Champions, Wrench now books online at 99% of its locations on ServiceTitan, and Authority Brands moved Punctual Pros and every other One Hour, Benjamin Franklin and Mister Sparky location onto ServiceTitan in September 2024. Fifth, they built recurring revenue that buyers pay for: Champions grew from about 60,000 members in 2021 to about 150,000 in 2026 (about 71 to 83 per technician) and sold to Blackstone in February 2026 at a reported ~18.5x trailing EBITDA, while Frontdoor gets 76% of its revenue from renewals with 84% of customers on auto-pay.Sixth, they owned the technician pipeline: Champions more than doubled its field technicians from 850 to 1,800+, Shermco grew certified technicians from 400+ to 600+ as Gryphon doubled revenue and sold for about $1.6B, and Sila bought a trade school in January 2026. Margin beat volume in the best compounders, as VWR grew Adjusted EBITDA 8.6% a year against 3.7% sales growth from 2006 to 2013 and IES grew operating income 88% on 21% more revenue in FY2024. In the last 12-18 months before a sale the winners kept buying and published KPIs: Shermco closed five add-ons in the 17 months before Blackstone, Sila added four brands in the nine months before Goldman's ~$1.7B (~17x) purchase, and Smith + Howard disclosed more than 600 employees and ~$175M of expected revenue about five months before TPG signed.Most exits went to a larger sponsor, often with the seller or management rolling equity (Charlesbank into GI Partners at ARS, Odyssey alongside Blackstone at Champions, BV alongside BSP at Frontline), and the median first-sponsor hold was about 4.4 years (4.0 in residential home services). The failures show what not to copy: Any Hour signed 16 partnerships in about 13 months and its loan now carries PIK at ~89% of par, TurnPoint grew from 17 to 65 brands and now pays PIK under a new CEO, Horizon is lender-supported, and Roto-Rooter's parent Chemed raised ad spend about $11M from 2023 to 2025 while segment revenue fell about $50M. For Punctual Pros the order is an integration leader and a ServiceTitan KPI pack now, members per technician as the north-star metric, one contiguous tuck-in per quarter in PA, NJ, MD and DE, a Lancaster academy with Thaddeus Stevens, leverage near the 2.9-3.3x lower-middle-market norm, and an exit-ready KPI pack by about 2028.Source: Value-creation case set synthesis, Oct 2026. Method and sources
How the cases were built, and where they are thin.

Method
17 residential home-services and franchisor histories and 17 cross-sector analogs (commercial and fire/life-safety services, legal services, lab distribution, agencies and consumer brands) were rebuilt from sponsor and company press releases, SEC filings, UK Companies House accounts, lender filings and trade press. Each case lists dated events, the levers used, before and after KPIs and what BSP can copy.
Levers and patterns were derived from the 237 dated events. Timing uses months from the first sponsor's entry; year-only dates count as mid-year. Evidence quality: 12 cases high (filings with disclosed figures), 17 medium (releases and trade press) and 5 low (few primary sources).
Unknown values stay blank and show as a dash. Figures from press reports, derived ratios and analyst recommendations carry an est. badge. All pages were retrieved Oct 6, 2026.

Caveats
Almost no sponsor discloses entry or exit EV, EBITDA or MOIC. The only exit multiples in the multiple fields are press estimates: Champions ~18.5x (Bloomberg-cited) and Sila ~17x incl. pending acquisitions (HomePros). Apex ~20x and FGS ~19x are analyst arithmetic and stay out of the multiple fields.revenue growth multiple uses only sourced before/after pairs or sponsor-stated multiples (TurnPoint ~10x, Smith + Howard ~4x, Sciens >35x, Shermco 2x, Teneo >2x); several are not like-for-like (perimeter changes, systemwide sales instead of revenue), as stated in each row note.Timing statistics are small samples: first add-on n=11, cadence n=8, hold n=21. First-add-on months exclude cases whose earliest add-ons are missing from the sources (e.g. Apex, Sila under MSCP, Heartland).Hold years measure the case's entry date to exit date, i.e. the first sponsor in the case fields (e.g. Odyssey for Champions, MSCP for Sila, GI Partners for Consilio).VWR and Avantor share the 2017 transaction; both are kept and cross-linked. Wrench and Apex share Alpine's growth plan. Smith + Howard also appears as template items in the nationwide plan.No case gives a sourced "share of customers on a membership" figure, so the membership pattern uses members per technician (Champions) and memberships per household served (Redwood/Sierra, derived).Vendor case studies (ServiceTitan, Rilla) and benchmarks cross-referenced from ServiceOS evidence and Punctual Pros nationwide plan are selected customers or vendor data, not controlled studies.Punctual Pros applicability, Punctual Pros next step and the Punctual Pros sequence are analyst recommendations, not company plans. Steps 0-2 are dated facts; steps 3-14 are proposed. Punctual Pros KPIs (members, booking rate, close rate) are not public and must come from its ServiceTitan.

How we estimated this

Staff: 96. From a company database search (ZoomInfo). Medium confidence.
Revenue: $18.4M est. Modelled by ZoomInfo, not reported. Check: 96 staff × $406K revenue per employee at listed electrical contractors = $39.0M ceiling; the estimate is 47% of that rate. Medium confidence.
EBITDA: $1.8M est. Revenue × 10%. Listed electrical peers earn 11.2% EBITDA margins (median); 10% assumed for a private contractor. Low confidence.
Likely price: $11.6M–$12.7M est. EBITDA × 6.3x to 6.9x, the average for deals under $25M of value (GF Data). The model starts at 6.5x: $12.0M. Low confidence.
Financing: $5.5M debt, $6.8M equity est. Debt of 3.0x EBITDA at 7.8%, the current market averages (GF Data), plus 3% deal fees. Market average.
Return: 16.1% a year est. Sold at the same 6.5x after 5 years, before any gain from merging into CET. Low confidence.

LabOS · for Thomas Scientific
Make every reorder digital. Make every account visible.
AI search that reads specs and CAS numbers, punchout, vendor-managed inventory and account-health scoring across 27,503 US lab sites. Mostly proven vendors, with a thin BSP data layer.
Terms: CAS number: a chemical's registry ID. Punchout: ordering from inside the customer's own purchasing system. VMI: vendor-managed inventory. ERP: the accounting and order system. PO: purchase order.
